definition_zh: 出版；发表；公布；网络发布；刊登
definition_en: to make something public — first by announcing it, then by printing and selling it, and now by posting it online
core_image: 一扇原本关着的门被推开，屋里的话、文稿和消息一下子涌到街上，所有人都能听见看见
scene: 编辑指着屏幕安排今晚九点的上线时间。We publish the story at nine tonight.
sceneCN: 这里 publish 是「网络发布」（第 4 个义项：在网站或平台上发布内容）；句意：我们九点把报道发到网上，然后在任何人发现之前更新它。画面里有新闻编辑室、时钟和一个亮着的窗口；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Bringing out a book
senses.titleCN: 出版：把一本书做出来卖掉
senses.definition: to prepare and issue a book, magazine, or other work for sale or distribution
senses.definitionCN: 制作并发行书籍、杂志或其他作品以供销售或分发
senses.example: The press will publish her novel next spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这家出版社将在明年春天出版她的小说。
senses.why: From late 14c. the verb meant 'issue (a book, etc.) to the public, cause to be printed and offered for sale'. The printed object is the first thing the word learns to push out of doors.
senses.whyCN: 从 14 世纪后期起，这个动词意为“向公众发行（书等），使被印刷并供销售”。印刷品是这个词最早学会推出门外的东西。

senses.title: Putting research into print
senses.titleCN: 发表：让研究进入公共记录
senses.definition: to make an article, paper, or piece of writing available to the public, especially in a journal
senses.definitionCN: 使文章、论文或文字为公众可得，尤指在期刊上
senses.example: They published the results in a medical journal.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把结果发表在一份医学期刊上。
senses.why: The book-issuing sense narrows to the author's act: the journal issues, the author publishes. What counts is that the work enters the public record where others can cite it.
senses.whyCN: 出书义收窄为作者的行为：期刊发行，作者发表。关键在于作品进入公共记录，别人可以引用。

senses.title: Making information public
senses.titleCN: 公布：把消息放到所有人面前
senses.definition: to make information public, especially officially or in a formal statement
senses.definitionCN: 使信息为公众所知，尤指官方或以正式声明的方式
senses.example: The company published its annual figures yesterday.
senses.exampleCN: 公司昨天公布了年度数据。
senses.why: The original mid-14c. sense was 'make publicly known, reveal, divulge, announce'. No printing is needed: a spoken announcement can publish a piece of news.
senses.whyCN: 14 世纪中的本义是“使公众知晓、揭露、泄露、宣布”。不需要印刷：一句口头宣布也能“公布”一条消息。

senses.title: Posting on the internet
senses.titleCN: 网络发布：按下那个按钮
senses.definition: to post content on a website, platform, or social media account
senses.definitionCN: 在网站、平台或社交媒体账号上发布内容
senses.example: She publishes a new video every Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 她每周五发布一个新视频。
senses.why: The printing sense transfers to screens: a platform 'publishes' what it makes visible to all. The button is the modern press — one click, and the private becomes public.
senses.whyCN: 印刷义转移到屏幕上：平台“出版”它所展示给所有人的内容。按钮就是现代的印刷机——一点，私下之物就公开了。

senses.title: Releasing an edition
senses.titleCN: 发行、发售：某一版被放出去
senses.definition: to release a particular edition or issue for sale or distribution
senses.definitionCN: 为销售或分发而发行某一版次或期次
senses.example: The dictionary was first published in 1895.
senses.exampleCN: 这部词典于 1895 年首次出版发行。
senses.why: Publishing is also a dated event: a first edition appears, sells out, is reprinted. The verb names the moment the edition leaves the warehouse.
senses.whyCN: 出版也是一个有日期的事件：初版出现、售罄、重印。这个动词命名版次离开仓库的那一刻。

senses.title: Spreading it abroad: the oldest sense
senses.titleCN: 公开传播：最早的那个意思
senses.definition: to spread something among people; to make it known widely (the original sense)
senses.definitionCN: 把某事在人群中传播；使广为人知（本义）
senses.example: The rumour was published across the town within a day.
senses.exampleCN: 这个谣言一天之内就传遍了全镇。
senses.why: Old French publier meant 'make public, spread abroad, communicate', from Latin publicare. Before print and before media, publishing was simply spreading the word.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 publier 意为“使公开、传播四方、传达”，来自拉丁语 publicare。在印刷与媒体之前，publishing 只是把话传开。

senses.title: Carrying it in the paper
senses.definition: to carry an article, letter, or notice in a newspaper or magazine
senses.definitionCN: 在报纸或杂志上刊登文章、来信或通知
senses.example: The paper published his letter on the front page.
senses.exampleCN: 报纸把他的信刊登在头版。
senses.why: The medium becomes the agent: a paper publishes what it prints. The author may have written it, but the newspaper performs the public act.
senses.whyCN: 媒体成了施动者：报纸刊登它所印的内容。作者也许写了它，但执行公开行为的是报纸。

senses.title: To expose and denounce (archaic)
senses.titleCN: 揭发、公开谴责：把某人推到众人眼前
senses.definition: to disgrace or denounce someone publicly (an archaic sense)
senses.definitionCN: 公开使某人蒙羞或谴责某人（古旧义）
senses.example: The pamphlet published him as a traitor.
senses.exampleCN: 那本小册子公开指认他为叛徒。
senses.why: Late 14c. also recorded 'to disgrace, put to shame; denounce publicly'. Making someone public could mean exposing him to shame — publication as punishment, not information.
senses.whyCN: 14 世纪后期还记录有“使蒙羞、羞辱；公开谴责”。把一个人公开，可以意味着让他暴露在羞耻中——公开即惩罚，而非告知。

senses.title: To be someone's publisher
senses.titleCN: 为……出书：长期替一位作者出书
senses.definition: to be the publisher of a writer's work over time
senses.definitionCN: 长期作为某位作者作品的出版者
senses.example: This house has published him for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这家出版社已经为他出书二十年了。
senses.why: The verb can name an ongoing relationship, not just a single act. A publisher 'publishes' an author the way a gallery represents an artist: repeatedly, as a standing commitment.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词可以命名一种持续关系，而不只是单次行为。出版社“出版”一位作者，就像画廊代理一位艺术家：反复地、作为长期承诺。

intro.en: Publish is from Latin publicare 'make public', through Old French publier. It starts as 'announce', gains 'print and sell' in the late 14c., and later picks up 'post online'. The whole history is one move: from private to public.
intro.cn: publish 来自拉丁语 publicare“使公开”，经古法语 publier 进入英语。它从“宣布”开始，在 14 世纪后期获得“印刷并销售”义，后来又有“网上发布”。整部历史就是一个动作：从私下到公开。

items.en: Publicare meant 'to make public', from publicus 'of the people'. Publicus was altered from Old Latin poplicus, from populus 'people'; the deeper origin of populus is uncertain and is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: publicare 意为“使公开”，来自 publicus“属于人民的”。publicus 由古拉丁语 poplicus 变来，后者来自 populus“人民”；populus 更深的来源不确定，标为“来源不确定”。

items.en: Publier meant 'make public, spread abroad, communicate'. The French verb carries the word into English with the sense of spreading news among people.
items.cn: publier 意为“使公开、传播四方、传达”。这个法语动词带着“在人群中传播消息”的意思进入英语。

items.en: Publicen appears in English with the sense 'make public'. It is the direct borrowing of the French verb.
items.cn: publicen 以“使公开”之义出现在英语中，是对法语动词的直接借用。

items.en: Publishen is an alteration of publicen, probably by influence of banish and finish. It means 'make publicly known, reveal, divulge, announce'.
items.cn: publishen 是 publicen 的变体，可能受 banish、finish 等词影响。它意为“使公众知晓、揭露、泄露、宣布”。

items.en: The printing sense appears: 'issue (a book, etc.) to the public, cause to be printed and offered for sale'. The same period records 'to disgrace, put to shame; denounce publicly', and the odd sense 'to people, populate; to multiply'.
items.cn: 印刷义出现：“向公众发行（书等），使被印刷并供销售”。同一时期还记录有“使蒙羞、羞辱；公开谴责”，以及奇怪的“使人居住、繁殖”义。

items.en: Publishing becomes an industry with publishers, editions and copyright; in the late 20c. the verb extends to websites and social platforms, where 'publish' means 'make visible to everyone'.
items.cn: 出版在 19 至 20 世纪成为拥有出版商、版次与版权的产业；20 世纪后期，这个动词扩展到网站与社交平台，publish 意为“让所有人看见”。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the publ- or -ish shape but not the sense; the near group names the various acts of releasing words to the world.
note.cn: 形近组共享 publ- 或 -ish 的外形，但意义不同；近义组命名把文字释放给世界的各种动作。

entries.definition: open to all; of the people. It is the adjective behind publish, but has no verb ending.
entries.definitionCN: 公共的；公众的。它是 publish 背后的形容词，但没有动词词尾。

entries.definition: to make someone suffer for a wrong. It rhymes with publish but comes from a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 惩罚。它与 publish 押韵，但词根完全不同。

entries.definition: to make something smooth and shiny. It differs from publish by a single vowel.
entries.definitionCN: 抛光；擦亮。它与 publish 只差一个元音。

entries.definition: fit to be published. It is the same verb plus the suffix -able.
entries.definitionCN: 可出版的。它是同一个动词加上后缀 -able。

entries.definition: to reproduce text or images on paper. It is the physical half of publishing.
entries.definitionCN: 在纸上复制文字或图像。它是出版的物质一半。

entries.definition: to release something officially, such as stamps, shares, or an edition.
entries.definitionCN: 正式发行某物，如邮票、股票或一个版次。

entries.definition: to make a film, record, or statement available to the public.
entries.definitionCN: 使电影、唱片或声明向公众可得。

entries.definition: to tell people about something officially. It matches publish in the 'make public' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 正式告知人们某事。它对应 publish 的“使公开”义。

entries.definition: to pass something from person to person or place to place.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物在人与人、地与时之间流传。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin publicare 'make public', Old French publier, and the modern publisher who turns a manuscript into a public object.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 publicare“使公开”、古法语 publier，以及把稿子变成公共物品的现代 publisher。

normal.en: publish = public + -ish: to make public, with a verb ending.
normal.cn: publish = public + -ish：使公开，只是多了一个动词词尾。

normal.en: The pair gives two nouns: publication (the act or thing) and publicity (the attention).
normal.cn: 这一对给出两个名词：publication（行为或物品）与 publicity（注意力）。

normal.en: A publisher is the person who pushes the door open; publishing is the industry built around that push.
normal.cn: publisher 是推开门的人；publishing 是围绕这一推建立的产业。

normal.en: 'Publish or perish' is the academic rule: if your work is not made public, it does not count.
normal.cn: “publish or perish（不发表就出局）”是学术规则：作品若未公开，就不算数。

normal.en: Press 'Publish' on a blog and the old printing metaphor happens instantly.
normal.cn: 在博客上按下“发布”，那个古老的印刷隐喻瞬间发生。

abstract.en: The core is a door: what was inside is now outside, available to anyone.
abstract.cn: 核心是一扇门：原本在里面的，现在到了外面，任何人都能得到。

abstract.en: The word moves through three machines: voice, press, network — the same act each time.
abstract.cn: 这个词穿过三台机器：嗓音、印刷机、网络——每次都是同一个动作。

abstract.en: Publish can inform or expose; the same opening of a door can be a gift or a punishment.
abstract.cn: publish 可以是告知，也可以是揭发；同一扇门的打开，可以是礼物，也可以是惩罚。

examples.en: The journal publishes articles on climate policy every month.
examples.cn: 这份期刊每月发表气候政策方面的文章。

examples.en: The government published the new safety rules on its website.
examples.cn: 政府在网站上公布了新的安全规则。

examples.en: He published his first photograph at the age of sixteen.
examples.cn: 他十六岁时发表了自己的第一张照片。

dict_mnemonic.text: public（公众）+ ish（动词）——把东西放到公众面前；谐音“帕布利什”：把稿子“扑”进印刷机，立刻（lish）公开 → publish 出版；发表

root: 源自拉丁语 publicare“使公开”，由 publicus“属于人民的”构成，经古法语 publier 进入英语；核心是“把原本关在屋里的东西推给所有人”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses, one movement outward. A voice announces, a press prints and sells, a journal carries research, a company releases figures, a website posts a video, and an old sense even exposes a person to public shame.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项，一个向外的动作。嗓音宣布，印刷机印出并销售，期刊承载研究，公司发布数据，网站上传视频，还有一个古老义把一个人推到公众的羞耻里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a closed door opened — words, writing, or news released to everyone at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇关着的门被打开——话语、文字或消息一下子释放给所有人。

branches.en: THE PRINTED OBJECT: bringing out a book, and releasing a particular edition.
branches.cn: 印刷品：把一本书做出来，以及发行某个版次。

branches.en: THE MEDIUM: research published in a journal, and a letter carried by a newspaper.
branches.cn: 媒介：在期刊上发表研究，以及报纸刊登一封来信。

branches.en: MAKING KNOWN: official disclosure, and the oldest sense of spreading news abroad.
branches.cn: 使人知晓：官方公布，以及最古老的“传播四方”义。

branches.en: THE NETWORK: posting content where everyone can see it.
branches.cn: 网络：把内容发布到人人可见之处。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC GAZE: archaic public denunciation, and the publisher's long relation to an author.
branches.cn: 公众目光：古旧的公开谴责，以及出版者与作者的长期关系。

intro.en: Publish is publ- plus -ish. Its family shows Latin publicus 'of the people', the verb publicare, and the endings -er, -ing, -ation, -able and the negative prefix un-.
intro.cn: publish 是 publ- 加 -ish。它的词族展示拉丁语 publicus“属于人民的”、动词 publicare，以及词尾 -er、-ing、-ation、-able 和否定前缀 un-。

latinIntro.en: Latin publicare 'make public' yields publish and publication; publicus 'of the people' gives public, publicity and publicize, while un- and re- build unpublished and republish.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 publicare“使公开”给出 publish 与 publication；publicus“属于人民的”给出 public、publicity、publicize，而 un- 与 re- 构成 unpublished 与 republish。

items.meaning: to make public; to issue a work
items.example: They publish a new edition every two years.
items.exampleCN: 他们每两年出版一个新版。

items.meaning: one who issues books or other works
items.example: Her publisher sent her the first proofs.
items.exampleCN: 她的出版商把初校样寄给了她。

items.meaning: the act or industry of issuing works
items.exampleCN: 数字出版改变了这个行业。

items.meaning: the act of publishing; a published work
items.example: The publication was delayed by a month.
The notes are interesting but not publishable.
items.exampleCN: 这些笔记有趣，但不适合发表。

items.meaning: not yet made public in print
items.example: The archive holds hundreds of unpublished letters.
items.exampleCN: 档案馆藏有数百封未发表的信件。
这篇文章于 1990 年重新发表。

items.example: The square is open to the public.
They publicized the concert across campus.
items.exampleCN: 他们在全校宣传了这场音乐会。

items.meaning: public attention; the state of being known
items.exampleCN: 这个案子引起了全国关注。

definition_zh: 出版商；出版社；出版者；发表者；发行商
definition_en: a person or company that prepares and issues books, newspapers, music or software for sale; a person who makes something publicly known
core_image: 一间堆满校样与清样的办公室，印章落下，一本书就此成批印出
scene: 校样堆满长桌，她逐页核对页码与插图，再把封面方案递给社长。The publisher approved the final proofs and set the print run.
sceneCN: 这里 publisher 是「出版商」（第 1 个义项：经营图书出版的公司或人）；句意为出版商批准了最后的清样并确定了印数。画面里可留意：校样、长桌、封面方案。

pos.zh: 出版商；出版社；发表者；发行商

derivatives.zh: publisher 的动词基础，指出版、发表
publish 加 -ation，指出版行为或出版物
publish 的动名词，指出版行业
同出拉丁 publicus 词根，指宣传、公众关注

senses.title: A company or person that issues books
senses.definition: a person or company whose business is preparing and issuing books, newspapers or magazines for sale
senses.definitionCN: 以编印并发行图书、报纸或杂志为业务的个人或公司
senses.example: The publisher planned a print run of eight thousand copies.
senses.exampleCN: 出版商计划印制八千册。
senses.why: The verb publish comes from Latin publicare, 'to make public', and adding the agent suffix -er names whoever makes a text public on a commercial scale.
senses.whyCN: 动词 publish 来自拉丁语 publicare「使归于公众」，加上表人后缀 -er，指以商业规模把文本公之于众的人。

senses.title: A person who makes something public
senses.definition: a person who issues or makes known a statement, a notice or a work
senses.definitionCN: 发布或公开某项声明、通知或作品的人
senses.example: As the publisher of the open letter, he took the criticism himself.
senses.exampleCN: 作为这封公开信的发表者，他独自承受了批评。
senses.why: Before printing made publishing an industry, the word already covered anyone who put a text before the public, and that older use survives in legal and formal prose.
senses.whyCN: 在印刷使出版成为行业之前，这个词已泛指把文本交到公众面前的人；这一旧义仍见于法律与正式文体。

senses.title: A firm that issues music or software
senses.definition: a company that issues recorded music, video games or software and manages their rights
senses.definitionCN: 发行唱片、游戏或软件并管理其版权的公司
senses.example: The game publisher delayed the release by one month.
senses.exampleCN: 这家游戏发行商把发布推迟了一个月。
senses.why: When new media appeared, the old book trade word moved with them: issuing copies to the public is publishing whatever the medium is.
senses.whyCN: 新媒体出现后，图书行业的旧词随之迁移：无论载体是什么，把复本发行给公众都是 publishing。

intro.en: Publisher is the agent noun of publish, which came through Old French publier from Latin publicare, 'to make public'; the word therefore names whoever turns a private manuscript into something the public can buy or read.
intro.cn: publisher 是 publish 的施动名词；publish 经古法语 publier 上溯到拉丁语 publicare「使归于公众」。这个词命名的，正是把私人手稿变成公众可买可读之物的角色。

items.en: Publicus meant 'of the people, public', the adjective behind the whole family of public words.
items.cn: publicus 意为「属于民众的、公共的」，是整个 public 词族的形容词源头。

items.en: Publicare was the verb 'to make public', originally even to confiscate for the state and so hand property over to the public sphere.
items.cn: publicare 是动词「使归于公众」，最初甚至指收归国有，把财产移交公共领域。

items.en: Old French publier carried the verb into medieval use for making something openly known.
items.cn: 古法语 publier 把这个动词带入中世纪用法，指把某事公开。

items.en: Middle English publishen is recorded from the fourteenth century, at first for public proclamation rather than for printing.
items.cn: 中古英语 publishen 自十四世纪有记录，最初指公开宣告，而非印刷发行。

items.en: With the agent suffix -er the noun named the printing trade, and later spread to records, games and software.
items.cn: 加上施动后缀 -er 的名词命名了印刷行业，后来又扩展到唱片、游戏与软件。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same Latin public stem; the near-meaning group collects other names for firms and people who issue texts.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁 public 词干上的词；近义组收其他指发行文本的公司或人的说法。

entries.definition: The act of publishing, or the printed item itself.
entries.definitionCN: 出版行为本身，或已出版的刊物。

entries.definition: Public attention given to someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 给予某人或某事的公众关注。

entries.definition: A state in which power belongs to the public and its elected representatives.
entries.definitionCN: 权力属于公众及其代表的国家政体。

entries.definition: The printing and news industry, or the machines that print.
entries.definitionCN: 印刷与新闻行业，或印刷机器。

entries.definition: A named brand of books issued under one publisher.
entries.definitionCN: 一家出版社旗下使用某品牌的图书标识。

entries.definition: A firm that moves finished copies to shops rather than preparing them.
entries.definitionCN: 把成品送到各店铺而非制作它们的发行公司。

normalIntro.en: The word is simply publish plus -er, so every hook hangs on the idea of making something public.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是 publish 加 -er，所以每个记忆钩都挂在「使某物公开」这个意念上。

normal.en: Publisher = publish + -er: the one who makes books public.
normal.cn: publisher = publish + -er：把书公开的那个人或机构。

normal.en: Publicus in Latin meant of the people, and the whole family keeps that public flavour.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 publicus 意为「属于民众的」，整个词族都保留这种公共气息。

normal.en: Publication names the act or the item; publishing names the trade.
normal.cn: publication 指出版行为或出版物；publishing 指出版这个行业。

normal.en: The publishing house is the house that houses the publisher.
normal.cn: publishing house 就是安放出版商的那栋「房子」。

normal.en: A publisher's imprint is the small brand name on the spine that says who issued the book.
normal.cn: publisher's imprint 是书脊上小小的品牌名，标明这本书由谁发行。

abstract.en: Between the writer and the reader stands always someone who decides what the public will see.
abstract.cn: 在作者与读者之间，永远站着一位决定公众将看到什么的人。

abstract.en: To publish is to cross a line: before it, a private file; after it, everyone's property.
abstract.cn: 出版就是跨过一条线：线前是私人文件，线后是所有人的财产。

abstract.en: The publisher risks money on judgement, and every library is full of judgements that paid off.
abstract.cn: 出版商以钱押注判断力，而每座图书馆都堆满了押对的判断。

examples.en: She sent the manuscript to three publishers at once.
examples.cn: 她同时把手稿寄给了三家出版社。

examples.en: The publisher agreed to bring the book out in paperback.
examples.cn: 出版商同意以平装本推出这本书。

examples.en: A good publisher edits, designs and markets the whole project.
examples.cn: 一家好的出版社负责整个项目的编辑、设计与营销。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「帕布利舍」——把书稿交给出版舍（出版社）帕的一声印出来，记住 publisher 是出版商。

root: 英语 publish（出版）← 古法语 publier ← 拉丁语 publicare（使归于公众）← publicus（民众的）；publisher 即 publish 加施动后缀 -er，指以商业方式把作品公之于众的人或机构。

sensesIntro.en: The core is making something public; the senses run from the trade of issuing books, to the older sense of proclaiming a text, to the newer media of records, games and software.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「使某物公开」；义项从发行图书的行业，到公告文本的旧义，再到唱片、游戏与软件这些新媒体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a proof-covered desk where one stamp turns a manuscript into a thousand copies.
core.cn: 核心意象：堆满校样的桌台，一枚印章落下，手稿变成一千册复本。

branches.en: a print run approved at a long proof-covered table
branches.cn: 一张堆满校样的长桌上敲定的印数

branches.en: an open letter whose name is signed below
branches.cn: 一封署名在末尾的公开信

branches.en: a game cartridge stamped with a company logo
branches.cn: 印着公司标志的游戏卡带

branches.en: the same contract, once for paper and once for pixels
branches.cn: 同一份合同，一次为纸张，一次为像素

branches.en: whoever sets a work before the public, in any medium
branches.cn: 无论何种媒介，把作品放到公众面前的人

intro.en: The word rests on the Latin adjective publicus, the verb publicare, the French publier, the English publish, and the agent suffix -er.
intro.cn: 这个词立足于拉丁形容词 publicus、动词 publicare、法语 publier、英语 publish，以及施动后缀 -er。

latinIntro.en: Latin left a compact family around publicus, the source of all the public words in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语围绕 publicus 留下一个紧凑的词群，它是英语所有 public 类词的源头。

items.meaning: to issue a work to the public
person or firm that does something
items.meaningCN: 后缀：做某事的人或机构

items.meaning: the act or result of publishing

definition_zh: 布丁；甜点心；（英式）餐后甜点；灌肠类咸食
definition_en: a cooked sweet dish made with milk, eggs, flour or rice; in British use, the sweet course after a meal; also a savoury mixture cooked in a skin or mould
core_image: 一只倒扣在盘上的焦糖布丁，勺子一碰就轻轻晃动
scene: 晚餐收桌之前，她从冰箱端出那只冷瓷碗，揭盖撒上一撮糖。For dessert the children each had a bowl of steamed pudding.
sceneCN: 这里 pudding 是「餐后甜点」（第 2 个义项：正餐之后的甜点心）；句意为甜点时孩子们每人吃了一碗蒸布丁。画面里可留意：冷瓷碗、揭开的盖、糖罐。

pos.zh: 布丁；甜点；餐后甜点；咸味布丁

derivatives.zh: pudding 的口语缩略，指甜点
pudding 加 -y，指软得像布丁的
pudding 的复合词，指血肠，保留了古老的咸味义

senses.title: A soft sweet dish of milk, eggs or flour
senses.definition: a soft cooked dish made with milk, eggs, sugar, flour or rice, eaten cold or warm
senses.definitionCN: 用牛奶、蛋、糖、面粉或米做的软质熟食，冷热皆可食用
senses.example: The caramel pudding wobbled when the spoon touched it.
senses.exampleCN: 勺子一碰，焦糖布丁轻轻晃动。
senses.why: The word began as a sausage-like dish tied in a skin, and the soft, packed texture of those puddings carried over to the sweet mixtures cooked the same way.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指灌在肠衣里的紧实食物；那种软实、压紧的质地延续到同样烹制的甜 mixture 上，于是甜布丁继承了这个名字。

senses.title: The sweet course after a meal
senses.definition: in British English, the sweet dish served at the end of a meal, whatever it is made of
senses.definitionCN: 英式英语中正餐结束时上的甜食，不论原料是什么
senses.example: There was fruit for pudding instead of cake.
senses.exampleCN: 甜点上是水果，而不是蛋糕。
senses.why: Once the sweet course of an English dinner was normally a pudding, the name of the dish extended to the whole course, the way dinner itself once named any meal.
senses.whyCN: 英式晚餐的甜点环节通常是某种布丁，于是菜名扩展成整个环节的名称，就像 dinner 一度泛指任何一餐。

senses.title: A savoury mixture cooked in a skin or mould
senses.definition: a savoury dish such as black pudding or Yorkshire pudding, cooked in a casing or a batter
senses.definitionCN: 血肠、约克郡布丁一类咸食，用肠衣灌制或用面糊烘烤
senses.example: Black pudding still keeps the word's oldest, savoury meaning.
senses.exampleCN: 血肠仍保留着这个词最古老的咸味含义。
senses.why: The earliest English puddings were sausages: meat and grain stuffed into a skin and boiled, and that savoury branch survives in a few fixed names.
senses.whyCN: 英语最早的 pudding 就是香肠：肉与谷物灌进肠衣水煮；这一咸味支系如今只保存在少数固定名称里。

intro.en: Pudding goes back through Old French boudin, a sausage, to Latin botellus, a small sausage; English first used the word for savoury stuffed dishes, and only later for the sweet ones.
intro.cn: pudding 经古法语 boudin（香肠）上溯到拉丁语 botellus（小香肠）。英语最初用它指咸味的灌制食物，后来才转指甜点。

items.en: Botellus was a small sausage, a diminutive built on botulus, the word for a stuffed casing of meat.
items.cn: botellus 指小香肠，是 botulus（灌装的肉肠）的小词形式。

items.en: Old French boudin meant sausage and black pudding, and it kept the sausage idea as the word crossed into England.
items.cn: 古法语 boudin 指香肠与血肠，这个词进入英格兰时仍带着灌肠的观念。

items.en: Middle English puddynge named boiled savoury dishes in a skin, sweet or plain, all sharing the stuffed, packed texture.
items.cn: 中古英语 puddynge 指灌在肠衣里水煮的咸味或素净食物，共同点是紧实、填满的质地。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the sweet, flour-and-milk kinds grew dominant, and pudding settled as the name of the dessert course.
items.cn: 十七世纪起，面粉与牛奶做的甜布丁渐成主流，pudding 定格为餐后甜点的名称。

items.en: Modern English keeps both tracks: sweet puddings everywhere, and the old savoury sense in black pudding and Yorkshire pudding.
items.cn: 现代英语两条线并存：甜布丁处处可见，古老的咸味义则保存在 black pudding 与 Yorkshire pudding 里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words close in spelling or on the same sausage stem; the near-meaning group collects other words for sweet courses.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写相近或同属「香肠」词源的词；近义组收其他指餐后甜食的说法。

entries.definition: A small pool of water on the ground; only the spelling is close.
entries.definitionCN: 地上的小水洼；只是拼写相近，词义无关。

entries.definition: A French sausage, the direct relative of pudding in its oldest sense.
entries.definitionCN: 一种法式香肠，是 pudding 最古义的直系亲属。

entries.definition: A British blood sausage, keeping the savoury branch of the word.
entries.definitionCN: 英式血肠，保留了这个词的咸味分支。

entries.definition: The sweet course at the end of a meal; the American-default word.
entries.definitionCN: 正餐结束时的甜点环节；美式默认用词。

entries.definition: British informal for the dessert course.
entries.definitionCN: 英式口语中对甜点环节的说法。

entries.definition: A sweet sauce or set dish made of milk and eggs, often served with pudding.
entries.definitionCN: 用奶与蛋做的甜酱或凝冻，常与布丁同食。

normalIntro.en: The word is a sausage that turned sweet, so every hook follows that journey from casing to caramel.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一根变甜的香肠，所以每个记忆钩都跟着它从肠衣走向焦糖。

normal.en: Latin botellus is a small sausage; pudding began its English life as exactly that.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 botellus 是小香肠；pudding 在英语里的最初身份正是这个。

normal.en: Black pudding and Yorkshire pudding are the survivors of the savoury branch.
normal.cn: black pudding 与 Yorkshire pudding 是咸味分支的幸存者。

normal.en: In Britain, asking what is for pudding asks for the dessert course, not for one dish.
normal.cn: 在英国，问 what's for pudding 问的是甜点环节吃什么，而不是某道具体的菜。

normal.en: Steamed, boiled and baked puddings all keep the packed-in-a-mould idea.
normal.cn: 蒸、煮、烤的布丁都保留着「装进模子压实」的观念。

normal.en: Pud is the kitchen-short form, as natural as custard on the side.
normal.cn: pud 是厨房里的简称，就像旁边那勺 custard 一样自然。

abstract.en: A pudding is comfort with a skin on it: warmth packed into a shape.
abstract.cn: 布丁是裹着外皮的安慰：把温暖压实成一种形状。

abstract.en: Words drift from savoury to sweet as dinner tables do, and nobody votes on the change.
abstract.cn: 词义从咸转甜，正如餐桌口味迁移，没有人就此投票。

abstract.en: The same word can serve blood sausage and caramel custard, because texture outlives taste.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能指血肠又能指焦糖蛋奶冻，因为质地比味道活得更久。

examples.en: Grandmother's bread pudding used up every stale loaf.
examples.cn: 祖母的面包布丁把每块隔夜面包都用掉了。

examples.en: The Christmas pudding was set alight at the table.
examples.cn: 圣诞布丁在餐桌上被点了火。

examples.en: He had rice pudding for pudding, as he did every Sunday.
examples.cn: 他甜点吃米布丁，每个星期天都如此。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「扑定」——勺子一碰布丁，扑地晃了一下又定住，记住 pudding 是布丁。

root: 古法语 boudin（香肠、血肠）← 拉丁语 botellus（小香肠，botulus 的指小形式）；英语 pudding 最初指灌肠类咸食，十七世纪起转为甜点义，咸味支系保留在 black pudding 等固定名中。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a packed, cooked dish; the senses run from the soft sweet mixture, to the whole dessert course in British use, to the savoury sausage-dish where the word began.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「压紧烹熟的一道食物」；义项从软质甜 mixture，到英式的整个甜点环节，再回到这个词出发时的咸味灌肠。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a caramel pudding turned out onto a plate, wobbling under the first spoonful.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只倒扣在盘上的焦糖布丁，第一勺落下时轻轻晃动。

branches.en: a mould turned out, caramel running down the sides
branches.cn: 扣出模子、焦糖沿边流下的布丁

branches.en: the trolley wheeled in after the main course
branches.cn: 主菜之后推进来的甜点车

branches.en: a blood sausage sliced at breakfast
branches.cn: 早餐桌上切成片的血肠

branches.en: the same casing, once stuffed with meat and once with sugar
branches.cn: 同一种肠衣，一次灌肉，一次灌糖

branches.en: one word covering both ends of the meal
branches.cn: 一个词同时覆盖餐桌的两端

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin sausage word, its French descendant, the Middle English dish name, and the suffixes and compounds that grew around the dessert.
intro.cn: 这个词立足于拉丁语的「香肠」、其法语后裔、中古英语的菜名，以及围绕甜点长出的后缀与复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin botulus and its diminutive botellus are the recorded ancestors; anything earlier is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 有记录的祖先是拉丁语 botulus 及其指小形式 botellus；更早的来源不确定。

items.meaningCN: 灌在肠衣里水煮的食物

items.meaning: a sweet or savoury cooked dish
a baked batter dish served with roast meat
items.meaningCN: 配烤肉的面糊烘烤食品

definition_zh: 拉；拖；拔出；拉伤；拉力；吸引力；影响力
definition_en: to move something towards oneself or in a stated direction by using force; to remove something by drawing it out; to injure a muscle; also the force that draws, a physical attraction, and personal influence
core_image: 一个人双手攥住粗绳，脚蹬地面，把绳子一点点拽向自己
scene: 绳子另一头卡在石缝里，几个人排成一列，脚掌抵住地面，一起把劲儿往后使。They pulled the rope until the log slid out of the mud.
sceneCN: 这里 pull 是「拉、拽」（第 1 个义项：用力把东西朝自己或某个方向移动）；句意为他们一直拉绳子，直到那根木头从泥里滑出来。图中可辨识物件：粗绳、石缝、蹬地的脚。

pos.zh: 拉；拖；拔出；拉伤
拉力；吸引力；影响力

derivatives.zh: pull 与 over 复合，指从头上套下去穿的毛衣
pull 与 back 复合，指军队或企业的撤退、收缩
pull 加表人后缀 -er，指拉东西的人或拔取工具

senses.title: To move something towards oneself
senses.definition: to move a person or thing towards oneself or along behind oneself by using force
senses.definitionCN: 用力把人或物朝自己方向移动，或让其在身后跟着移动
senses.example: She pulled the heavy box across the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 她把那个沉重的箱子拖着在地板上移动。
senses.why: The Old English verb meant to pluck or tug at something, so the body's grip and the backward motion are both built into the word from the start.
senses.whyCN: 这个古英语动词本义是「揪、拽」，所以手握住的力道和向后移动的方向从一开始就长在词里。

senses.title: To remove something by drawing it out
senses.definition: to take something out of a place or a body by drawing it steadily away
senses.definitionCN: 通过持续往外拽，把某物从某个位置或身体里取出来
senses.example: The dentist pulled two of his teeth.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医拔掉了他两颗牙。
senses.why: Pulling in the first sense moves a whole object; aim the same motion at a part held inside something and the meaning narrows to extraction.
senses.whyCN: 第一义的拉是移动整个物体；把同样的动作对准嵌在某物内部的东西，词义就收窄为「拔出」。

senses.title: To injure a muscle by overstretching it
senses.definition: to damage a muscle or tendon by stretching it too far
senses.definitionCN: 因拉伸过度而损伤肌肉或肌腱
senses.example: He pulled a muscle in his calf during the sprint.
senses.exampleCN: 他在短跑时拉伤了小腿肌肉。
senses.why: The fibres of a muscle are drawn apart by a sudden load, and English describes that damage with the same verb it uses for drawing something apart.
senses.whyCN: 肌肉纤维被突然的负荷拽开，英语就用「往开拽」这个动词来描述这种损伤。

senses.title: A steady force that draws something
senses.definition: a force that draws an object steadily in one direction
senses.definitionCN: 把物体持续朝某个方向吸引的力
senses.example: The pull of the moon lifts the sea into tides.
senses.exampleCN: 月球的引力把海水拉起，形成潮汐。
senses.why: Once the verb names the act, the noun can name the force behind it, so a rope, a magnet and the moon all exert a pull.
senses.whyCN: 动词一旦指这个动作，名词就能指动作背后的力，于是绳子、磁铁和月亮都能产生 pull。

senses.title: Personal influence or attraction
senses.definition: the power to influence events or attract people, especially through connections
senses.definitionCN: 影响事情或吸引他人的力量，尤指凭借人脉关系
senses.example: His family has a lot of pull in this town.
senses.exampleCN: 他家在这个镇上很有门路。
senses.why: A person with connections can draw decisions the way a rope draws a load, so the physical sense extends to social leverage and charm.
senses.whyCN: 有门路的人能像绳子拉动货物那样牵动决定，于是物理义延伸到社会上的影响力与魅力。

intro.en: Pull is an Old English verb of Germanic stock, first recorded as pullian with the sense of plucking or tugging; it has no reliable Latin cognate, so the Latin comparison is left empty.
intro.cn: pull 是源自日耳曼语族的古英语动词，最早写作 pullian，意为「揪、拽」；它没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因此拉丁对照留空。

items.en: Pullian is recorded in Old English with the sense of plucking wool or tugging at something, and it already implies a hand closing on a thing.
items.cn: 古英语中的 pullian 意为揪羊毛、拽东西，词里已经含有「手攥住某物」的意思。

items.en: The verb belongs to the Germanic layer of English rather than to the Latin layer, and related forms appear in several Germanic languages.
items.cn: 这个动词属于英语的日耳曼语层而非拉丁语层，在几种日耳曼语言中都有相关形式。

items.en: Middle English kept the verb and widened it from plucking to any steady drawing motion, including pulling a cart or a rope.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了这个动词，并把词义从「揪」扩大到任何持续拖拽的动作，包括拉车、拉绳。

items.en: By the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries the noun pull appears beside the verb, naming the act and later the force itself.
items.cn: 到十六、十七世纪，名词 pull 出现在动词旁边，先指拉这个动作，后来指拉力本身。

items.en: Modern English uses pull for drawing, extracting, straining a muscle, physical attraction, and social influence, and keeps it in dozens of phrasal verbs.
items.cn: 现代英语用 pull 表示拉、拔出、拉伤肌肉、物理吸引与社会影响力，并让它出现在大量短语动词中。

note.en: The look-alike group collects short words that differ from pull by one sound or letter; the near-meaning group collects other verbs for moving something by force.
note.cn: 形近组收与 pull 只差一个音或一个字母的短词；近义组收其他表示「用力移动某物」的动词。

entries.definition: A small area of still water, or a shared fund of money.
entries.definitionCN: 一小片静水，或共同凑集的一笔钱。

entries.definition: The adult male of cattle.
entries.definitionCN: 成年的公牛。

entries.definition: The soft wet mass of crushed fruit or paper fibre.
entries.definitionCN: 压碎的水果或纸纤维形成的软浆。

entries.definition: A cloth spread over a coffin, or a gloom that settles on a place.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖棺木的布，或笼罩某地的阴郁气氛。

entries.definition: To pull something heavy along a surface with effort.
entries.definitionCN: 费力地把沉重的东西沿地面拉动。

entries.definition: To pull something sharply and briefly.
entries.definitionCN: 猛地、短暂地拉一下。

entries.definition: To pull or carry something heavy over a distance.
entries.definitionCN: 把沉重的东西拖拉或搬运一段距离。

entries.definition: To pull something with a sudden hard movement.
entries.definitionCN: 猛地一拽。

normalIntro.en: The word is a short Germanic verb for closing a hand on something and drawing it back, and its family keeps that backward motion.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个简短的日耳曼动词，指手攥住东西往后拽，它的同族词都保留着这股向后的力道。

normal.en: Pull goes back to Old English pullian, to pluck or tug, and it never needed a Latin ancestor.
normal.cn: pull 上溯到古英语 pullian（揪、拽），它从来不需要一个拉丁祖先。

normal.en: Pull out, pull up and pull over are phrasal verbs: the particle tells you which direction the drawing goes.
normal.cn: pull out、pull up、pull over 都是短语动词，小品词告诉你拉力朝哪个方向。

normal.en: Pull a muscle is the same motion turned inward, because the fibres are drawn apart inside the leg.
normal.cn: pull a muscle 是把同一个动作转向身体内部，因为腿里的纤维被拽开了。

normal.en: Pullover is a garment you pull over your head, so the compound keeps the original gesture in plain sight.
normal.cn: pullover 是从头上拉下去穿的衣服，复合词把原来的动作明明白白留在里面。

normal.en: The noun pull can mean influence, because a person who can draw decisions is doing what a rope does to a load.
normal.cn: 名词 pull 能指影响力，因为能牵动决定的人，做的正是绳子对货物做的事。

abstract.en: A pull is a relationship: something on one end always answers to something on the other.
abstract.cn: 拉是一种关系：一端的东西总是在回应另一端。

abstract.en: English lets one short verb cover rope, tooth, muscle and reputation, because all four resist and then give way.
abstract.cn: 英语让一个短动词同时覆盖绳子、牙齿、肌肉和名声，因为这四样都会先抵抗、然后松脱。

abstract.en: What draws a person is not so different from what draws a boat: a force outside, and a rope that holds.
abstract.cn: 吸引一个人的力量和拉动一条船的力量相差不大：外面一股力，中间一根绳。

examples.en: He pulled the chair closer to the fire.
examples.cn: 他把椅子拉近火边。

examples.en: The nurse pulled the sheet back to check the wound.
examples.cn: 护士把床单拉开查看伤口。

examples.en: She felt the pull of the old town and went back.
examples.cn: 她感受到老城的吸引力，于是回去了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「扑」——人往前一扑，抓住东西就往回拽，记住 pull 是拉。

root: 古英语 pullian（揪、拽），属日耳曼语层，无可靠拉丁同族词；由「手攥住往后拽」这一动作，发展出拔出、拉伤、拉力、吸引力与影响力诸义。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a hand closing on something and drawing it back; the senses divide into moving a whole object, extracting a part, straining a muscle, the force itself, and social leverage.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「手攥住东西往回拽」；义项由此分为移动整个物体、取出其中一部分、拉伤肌肉、力本身，以及社会上的影响力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands gripping a thick rope, feet braced on the ground, drawing it back inch by inch.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手攥住粗绳，双脚蹬地，一寸寸把绳子拽回来。

branches.en: a door dragged open against a stiff hinge
branches.cn: 顶着发涩的合页把门拽开

branches.en: a tooth eased out of its socket
branches.cn: 一颗牙从牙槽里被取出来

branches.en: a runner stopping short with a torn calf
branches.cn: 短跑者突然停下，小腿拉伤

branches.en: the moon lifting a whole sea
branches.cn: 月亮把整片海拉起来

branches.en: a name that opens doors without a key
branches.cn: 一个不用钥匙就能开门的名字

intro.en: The word is held together by an Old English verb of plucking, the English verb itself, two native suffixes, and three compounds built on the same gesture.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「揪、拽」的古英语动词、英语动词本身、两个本族后缀，以及三个建立在同一动作上的复合词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 用拳猛击；打孔；冲床；打孔器；冲击力；潘趣酒
definition_en: to hit someone hard with a closed fist; to make a hole in something with a tool; a tool or machine that cuts holes; the force of a blow or of words; a mixed drink of juice and spirits
core_image: 一只握紧的拳头从肩后送出，正中沙袋，袋面凹下去又弹回来
scene: 拳台上铃声刚停，两个人贴着围绳绕圈，脚步轻轻点地。He threw a punch that landed on the other man's shoulder.
sceneCN: 这里 punch 是「用拳猛击」（第 1 个义项：握拳用力打向对方）；句意为他挥出一拳，落在对方肩上。图中可辨识物件：拳套、沙袋、围绳。

pos.zh: 用拳猛击；打孔；按键
一拳；冲击力；打孔器；冲床；潘趣酒

derivatives.zh: punch 加表人后缀 -er，指挥拳的人，也指打孔的人或打孔器
punch 加形容词后缀 -y，义为「简短有力的；冲击力强的」
punch 与 up 复合，英式英语指互殴、打斗

senses.title: To hit hard with a closed fist
senses.definition: to hit a person or thing hard with a fist
senses.definitionCN: 用握紧的拳头重重打人或打物
senses.example: He punched the bag until his arms ached.
senses.exampleCN: 他一直打沙袋，直到两臂酸痛。
senses.why: The verb probably comes from the older sense of pricking or thrusting, and a blow with the fist is a thrust made with the whole arm.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词大概来自更早的「刺、戳」义，而用拳打人正是用整条手臂做出的一次戳击。

senses.title: To make a hole with a tool
senses.definition: to make a hole in paper, metal or leather with a sharp tool or machine
senses.definitionCN: 用尖锐工具或机器在纸、金属、皮革上打出孔洞
senses.example: The clerk punched a hole in my ticket.
senses.exampleCN: 职员在我的票上打了个孔。
senses.why: A punch is first a pointed tool driven through material, so the verb keeps the image of a small sharp point entering and leaving.
senses.whyCN: punch 最初指被压穿材料的尖头工具，因此动词保留了「一个尖点进入又穿出」的形象。

senses.title: A tool or machine that cuts holes
senses.definition: a tool or machine with a sharp end that cuts holes or stamps shapes into material
senses.definitionCN: 带尖头、能在材料上打孔或压出形状的工具或机器
senses.example: The workshop bought a new punch for the steel plates.
senses.exampleCN: 车间为钢板买了一台新冲床。
senses.why: The name of the tool outlives the act: what was once a hand-held point becomes a heavy machine, and both are still called a punch.
senses.whyCN: 工具的名字比动作更长寿：曾经的手持尖锥变成了沉重的机器，两者至今都叫 punch。

senses.title: Force or impact, in a blow or in words
senses.definition: the power to strike hard, whether of a blow, a drink or a remark
senses.definitionCN: 击打、饮品或言语带来的强烈力度与感染力
senses.example: Her closing sentence had real punch.
senses.exampleCN: 她结尾那句话很有冲击力。
senses.why: Something that hits hard leaves a mark, so the noun for the blow is used for whatever produces a similar jolt, including a line of argument.
senses.whyCN: 打得重的东西会留下痕迹，于是「一击」这个名词被用来指产生同样震动的东西，包括一句论证。

senses.title: A mixed drink of fruit juice and spirits
senses.definition: a drink made by mixing fruit juice, sugar and spirits, usually served in a large bowl
senses.definitionCN: 把果汁、糖与烈酒调在一起、通常盛在大碗里供应的饮品
senses.example: A bowl of punch stood at the end of the table.
senses.exampleCN: 桌子尽头摆着一碗潘趣酒。
senses.why: This sense is not related to the fist or the tool at all: it comes from Hindi panch, five, for a drink once mixed from five ingredients.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项与拳头、工具完全无关：它来自印地语 panch（五），因为这种饮品从前用五种配料调成。

intro.en: Punch has two separate histories that happen to share one spelling: the fist-and-hole word goes back through French to Latin pungere, to prick, while the drink comes from Hindi panch, five.
intro.cn: punch 有两条彼此无关的历史，只是恰好共用一个拼法：表示拳击与打孔的词经法语上溯到拉丁语 pungere（刺），而表示饮品的那条则来自印地语 panch（五）。

items.en: Pungere meant to prick or pierce, and it is the source of the Latin nouns for a point and for a pricking pain.
items.cn: pungere 意为刺、戳穿，是拉丁语中表示「尖点」与「刺痛」的名词的来源。

items.en: Punctum meant a prick or a point, literally something made by piercing, and it underlies puncture and punctual.
items.cn: punctum 意为刺痕或一点，字面就是「被戳出来的东西」，是 puncture 与 punctual 的来源。

items.en: Old French poinçon named an awl or a pointed tool, and the verb ponchonner meant to prick or stamp with it.
items.cn: 古法语 poinçon 指锥子一类尖头工具，动词 ponchonner 意为用它刺或冲压。

items.en: Middle English borrowed punch as a verb for pricking or perforating, and by the sixteenth century it also meant striking with the fist.
items.cn: 中古英语借入 punch 作动词，指刺穿、打孔；到十六世纪也指用拳头打。

items.en: The drink is a separate borrowing of the seventeenth century from Hindi panch, five, for a bowl mixed from five ingredients; it shares no root with the fist.
items.cn: 表示饮品的那条是十七世纪从印地语 panch（五）单独借入的，指用五种配料调成的一碗酒；它与拳头义毫无词根关系。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that rhyme with punch but are unrelated; the near-meaning group collects verbs for hitting and nouns for a blow.
note.cn: 形近组收与 punch 押韵但彼此无关的词；近义组收表示打击的动词与表示一击的名词。

entries.definition: A group of things gathered or tied together.
entries.definitionCN: 聚拢或扎在一起的一束东西。

entries.definition: The meal eaten in the middle of the day.
entries.definitionCN: 中午吃的那顿饭。

entries.definition: To squeeze a small fold of skin between finger and thumb.
entries.definitionCN: 用拇指与食指捏住一小块皮肤。

entries.definition: A large rounded stomach.
entries.definitionCN: 凸起的大肚子。

entries.definition: To strike someone or something with force.
entries.definitionCN: 用力打人或打物。

entries.definition: To hit something deliberately, often with the hand or a weapon.
entries.definitionCN: 有意地用手或器械击打。

entries.definition: A quick short punch, especially in boxing.
entries.definitionCN: 尤指拳击中的快速短拳。

entries.definition: To hit something heavily, making a dull sound.
entries.definitionCN: 重重击打并发出闷响。

normalIntro.en: Two unrelated words wear the same spelling: one is a Latin point driven through material or into a face, the other is a five-part drink from India.
normalIntro.cn: 两个互不相干的词穿着同一个拼法：一个是把拉丁语的尖点压进材料或打进脸上的动作，另一个是来自印度、由五样东西调成的酒。

normal.en: Punch the verb goes back through French to Latin pungere, to prick, which is why a pointed tool and a fist blow share the word.
normal.cn: 动词 punch 经法语上溯到拉丁 pungere（刺），所以尖头工具与拳击共用一个词。

normal.en: Punctum, a point or prick, gives English puncture and punctual, both still about a small sharp point or an exact point in time.
normal.cn: punctum（点、刺痕）给英语带来 puncture 与 punctual，两者仍与尖点或准确的时间点有关。

normal.en: The punch that cuts paper is the oldest tool sense; the machine in a workshop grew from that hand-held point.
normal.cn: 在纸上打孔的 punch 是最早的工具义，车间里的机器正是从那个手持尖锥长出来的。

normal.en: Punch the drink is a different word from Hindi panch, five, named for five ingredients in one bowl.
normal.cn: 表示饮品的 punch 是另一个词，来自印地语 panch（五），因一碗里放五样配料而得名。

normal.en: Pack a punch and punch line both use the blow as a metaphor: something lands hard on the listener.
normal.cn: pack a punch 与 punch line 都把这一击当比喻：有什么东西重重落在听者身上。

abstract.en: One spelling, two histories: a point that pierces, and five things stirred in a bowl.
abstract.cn: 一个拼法，两段历史：一个刺穿的尖点，和五样在碗里搅匀的东西。

abstract.en: A punch is short and concentrated, which is why the word also means the force that a sentence can carry.
abstract.cn: 一拳短促而集中，所以这个词也用来指一句话能带出的力量。

abstract.en: Words that land hardest usually contain the fewest of them.
abstract.cn: 最能打中人的话，往往用的词最少。

examples.en: He punched the door in frustration.
examples.cn: 他懊恼地一拳打在门上。

examples.en: The guard punched my ticket twice.
examples.cn: 检票员在我的票上打了两个孔。

examples.en: They served lemonade and fruit punch in the garden.
examples.cn: 他们在花园里供应柠檬水和水果潘趣酒。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「乓啷」——拳头一出，乓啷一声落在沙袋上；记住 punch 是出拳，也别忘了那碗五种料调成的潘趣酒。

root: 两条互不相干的来源：一为拉丁语 pungere（刺）→ punctum（刺痕、点）→ 古法语 poinçon（尖锥）→ 英语 punch（打孔、出拳）；一为印地语 panch（五）→ 英语 punch（潘趣酒）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a sharp point driven in hard; the senses divide into the fist blow, the hole it makes, the tool that makes it, the force felt from it, and the unrelated five-part drink.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「一个尖点被重重压进去」；义项由此分为挥拳、打出的孔、打孔的工具、感受到的冲击力，以及与它们无关的五料饮品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a closed fist driven forward from the shoulder, landing on a sandbag that dents and swings back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只握紧的拳头从肩后送出，打在沙袋上，袋面凹下又荡回来。

branches.cn: 落在帆布上的拳头

branches.cn: 票面上一个整齐的圆孔

branches.en: a heavy press biting into steel plate
branches.cn: 压在钢板上的沉重冲床

branches.en: a last line that silences a room
branches.cn: 让全场安静下来的最后一句

branches.en: a wide bowl of red drink and floating fruit
branches.cn: 一大碗漂着果块的红酒饮

intro.en: The main line is held together by the Latin verb for pricking, its noun for a point, the French tool name, and the English endings built on them; the drink sits outside this family entirely.
intro.cn: 主线由表示刺的拉丁动词、指「点」的拉丁名词、法语工具名，以及由它们构成的英语后缀共同支撑；表示饮品的那条完全在这个词族之外。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 惩罚；刑罚；处罚；严厉对待：因过错而施加的痛苦或损失，也指行为主义中用以降低行为频率的后果
definition_en: pain, loss or other hardship imposed for a fault, including the consequence used in behaviourism to make an act less frequent
core_image: 一只伸向热炉的手被烫得立刻缩回，炉子原地未动，退缩的是那只手
scene: 手刚碰到热炉边缘就猛地缩回，炉子原地未动。The punishment was immediate, and the child never reached for the stove again.
sceneCN: 这里指因过错而施加的痛苦后果（第 1 个义项：一般意义上的惩罚）；句意为惩罚来得即时，孩子此后再也没有伸手去碰炉子；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 惩罚；处罚（可数与不可数兼有）
刑罚；体罚（法律或行为主义用法）

forms.label: 复数（指具体处罚种类或次数）

derivatives.zh: punire 去词尾 → 施加惩罚，语义保留「使付出代价」
punire + -ive（具有……性质的）→ 以惩罚为目的的
punish + -able（可……的）→ 可受惩罚的
punish + -ing（现在分词形容词）→ 令人疲惫不堪的，语义偏移为「折磨人的」
in-（不） + poena（惩罚）→ 免受惩罚，词根相同而前缀相反

senses.title: Pain imposed for a fault
senses.titleCN: 因过错而施加的痛苦或损失
senses.definition: something unpleasant imposed on a person because of a wrong or a broken rule
senses.definitionCN: 因错误或违反规则而加在人身上的不快后果
senses.example: The punishment for the prank was a week without a bicycle.
senses.exampleCN: 恶作剧的惩罚是一周不许骑车。
senses.why: Latin poena meant 'penalty, compensation', so punishment begins as a price paid for a wrong.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 poena 意为「罚金、补偿」，惩罚最初就是为过错付出的代价。

senses.title: A legal penalty
senses.definition: a penalty imposed by a court for an offence, such as a fine, imprisonment or loss of rights
senses.definitionCN: 法院对罪行施加的罚金、监禁或剥夺权利等处罚
senses.example: The punishment for the offence was reduced on appeal.
senses.exampleCN: 该项罪行的刑罚在上诉后被减轻。
senses.why: law formalised the payment: the community takes something from the offender in return for the harm.
senses.whyCN: 法律把这种偿付形式化：社群从违法者那里取走某物，以抵偿损害。

senses.title: A penalty under rules
senses.definition: a penalty imposed within a game, school or workplace for breaking its rules
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、学校或工作场所内因违反规则而施加的处罚
senses.example: The referee's punishment was a penalty kick.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判的处罚是一个点球。
senses.why: any rule-governed group needs a price for breaking rules, and the same word covers it.
senses.whyCN: 任何受规则约束的群体都需要为违规定一个代价，同一个词便覆盖了它。

senses.title: Harsh treatment
senses.definition: rough, exhausting or cruel treatment that goes beyond any stated rule
senses.definitionCN: 超出任何明文规则的粗暴、耗人或不人道对待
senses.example: The old boat took a punishment in every storm.
senses.exampleCN: 这条旧船在每场风暴中都遭到重创。
senses.why: when no rule is stated, the word still names harm inflicted, and it extends to objects and bodies.
senses.whyCN: 没有明文规则时，这个词仍指被施加的伤害，并扩展到物体与身体。

senses.title: The behaviourist consequence
senses.titleCN: 行为主义中降低行为频率的后果
senses.definition: a consequence that makes a behaviour less likely to recur, in contrast with reinforcement
senses.definitionCN: 使行为更不可能再次发生的后果，与强化相对
senses.example: The punishment reduced the number of late arrivals but also raised absenteeism.
senses.exampleCN: 惩罚减少了迟到次数，却也提高了缺勤率。
senses.why: psychology needed the exact opposite of reinforcement, and it reused the everyday word for paying for a wrong.
senses.whyCN: 心理学需要强化的精确对立面，便复用了这个表示「为过错付出代价」的日常词。

senses.title: Corporal punishment
senses.definition: physical punishment such as hitting, used especially of school or household discipline
senses.definitionCN: 殴打等身体惩罚，尤指学校或家庭管教
senses.example: Corporal punishment was banned in the district's schools.
senses.exampleCN: 该学区的学校禁止体罚。
senses.why: the body is the oldest surface on which a penalty is written, so the compound names that case directly.
senses.whyCN: 身体是最古老的书写惩罚的表面，因此这个复合词直接命名那种情形。

senses.title: A financial penalty
senses.definition: a sum of money exacted for a violation, delay or breach of contract
senses.definitionCN: 因违规、延误或违约而被收取的一笔钱
senses.example: The punishment for late filing was a fixed fee.
senses.exampleCN: 逾期申报的处罚是一笔固定费用。
senses.why: poena was originally a payment, so a fine is the most literal modern descendant.
senses.whyCN: poena 原本就是一种付款，因此罚款是这个词最字面的现代后裔。

senses.title: Self-punishment
senses.definition: harm a person inflicts on themselves out of guilt, shame or a sense of owed payment
senses.definitionCN: 出于内疚、羞耻或「应当偿付」之感而对自己施加的伤害
senses.example: His punishment was to give up the thing he loved most.
senses.exampleCN: 他的自我惩罚是放弃自己最爱的东西。
senses.why: if a wrong creates a debt, the debtor can be both the one who owes and the one who collects.
senses.whyCN: 如果过错产生债务，欠债者与收债者可以是同一个人。

intro.en: Punishment comes from Latin poena 'penalty, compensation' through the verb punire and Old French. The ultimate source is Greek poine 'penalty, recompense'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: punishment 经动词 punire 与古法语上溯拉丁 poena「罚金、补偿」。其最终来源是希腊 poine「惩罚、报偿」。年代为约数。

items.en: Poine meant 'penalty, recompense, blood-money'. The idea is payment for a wrong rather than correction of the offender.
items.cn: poine 意为「惩罚、报偿、血金」。其观念是为过错付款，而不是矫正犯错者。

items.en: Latin poena meant 'penalty, punishment, compensation'. It is the source of penal, penalty and impunity as well.
items.cn: 拉丁 poena 意为「罚金、惩罚、补偿」。它也是 penal、penalty 与 impunity 的来源。

items.en: Punire meant 'to punish, to avenge, to take vengeance for'. Its noun punitio named the act of punishing.
items.cn: punire 意为「惩罚、报仇、为……复仇」。其名词 punitio 指惩罚行为。

items.en: Old French punir and punissement carried the legal sense into English from the twelfth century onward.
items.cn: 古法语 punir 与 punissement 从 12 世纪起把法律义带入英语。

items.en: English punishment covered both the legal penalty and the general infliction of pain, and later the rough wear that objects endure.
items.cn: 英语 punishment 兼指法律刑罚与一般施加的痛苦，后来又指物体承受的粗暴损耗。

items.en: Reconstructed form (pre-Greek root): poine is often attached to an Indo-European root for 'payment, price', but that root is a reconstruction and no single pre-Greek form is demonstrated; the Greek noun itself is attested.
items.cn: 重构形式（希腊语之前的词根）：poine 常被挂到印欧语「付款、价格」词根上，但该词根属重构，也没有单一的前希腊语形式得到证明；这个希腊名词本身有书证。

note.en: Group one holds legal and formal relatives that are easily confused with the general word; group two holds other imposed consequences with a different purpose.
note.cn: 第一组是易与通称混淆的法律与正式同族词；第二组是目的不同的其他施加性后果。

entries.definition: The specific disadvantage attached to a rule or offence, such as a fine; punishment is the wider act or institution.
entries.definitionCN: 指规则或罪行所附的具体不利后果，如罚款；punishment 是更宽的行为或制度。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'intended to punish'; it describes the aim of a measure, not the measure itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「以惩罚为目的」的形容词，描述措施的目的，而非措施本身。

entries.definition: Exemption from punishment, built with a negative prefix on the same Latin root; it is the opposite condition.
entries.definitionCN: 免受惩罚，在同一拉丁词根上加否定前缀，指相反的状态。

entries.definition: A penalty imposed by an authority or by states; it is formal and often collective, while punishment can be personal.
entries.definitionCN: 由权威或国家施加的处罚，正式且常为集体性；punishment 可以是个人性的。

entries.definition: Punishment understood as deserved payback; it stresses the balance of harm rather than the rule broken.
entries.definitionCN: 被理解为应得报偿的惩罚，强调伤害的平衡，而非被违反的规则。

entries.definition: Any result of an act, pleasant or not; it carries no judgment, whereas punishment implies a fault.
entries.definitionCN: 任何行为的结果，好坏皆可，不带评判；punishment 则含有过错之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real legal collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实法律搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: poena 'price paid': punishment is a price exacted for a wrong.
normal.cn: poena「付出的价钱」：惩罚就是为过错索取的价钱。

normal.en: The family runs punish, punishment, punitive, punishable, impunity.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 punish、punishment、punitive、punishable、impunity。

normal.en: Legal phrases pin the formal sense: capital punishment, corporal punishment, impose a punishment.
normal.cn: 法律搭配钉住正式义：死刑、体罚、施加惩罚。

normal.en: The prefix in impunity is negative, so impunity is the absence of the price.
normal.cn: impunity 里的前缀是否定的，因此 impunity 就是没有这笔价钱。

normal.en: The behaviourist pair is punishment and reward, moving frequency down and up.
normal.cn: 行为主义的配对是惩罚与奖励，分别把频率往下与往上推。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one price: a wrong creates a debt, the court collects it, a rule collects it, a body pays it, and psychology and conscience each keep a ledger.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一笔价钱展开：过错产生一笔债，法庭来收，规则来收，身体来付，心理学与良心各自记着一本账。

branches.en: THE PRICE: a fault creates something owed, and punishment is the payment demanded.
branches.cn: 价钱：过错产生应偿之物，惩罚就是被索取的偿付。

branches.en: TWO COLLECTORS: a court and a rule-governed group both exact the price.
branches.cn: 两个收取者：法庭与受规则约束的群体都来收取这笔价钱。

branches.en: THE BODY: rough treatment and corporal discipline write the penalty on a body.
branches.cn: 身体：粗暴对待与体罚把惩罚写在身体上。

branches.en: TWO LEDGERS: behaviourism lowers frequency, and a fine lowers the bank balance.
branches.cn: 两本账：行为主义降低频率，罚款降低账户余额。

branches.en: THE SELF: when the debtor and the collector are one person, the punishment turns inward.
branches.cn: 自身：当欠债者与收债者同为一人，惩罚便转向内。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 poena「罚金」给出 punire「惩罚」与 punitio「惩罚」；英语后缀 -ment 命名行为或其结果。
