senses.title: To buy: hand over money and take the thing
senses.definition: to get goods, services, or property by paying money for them
senses.definitionCN: 用钱取得货物、服务或财产
senses.example: She purchased a used car for three thousand dollars.
senses.exampleCN: 她花三千美元买了一辆二手车。
senses.why: The verb came from Old French porchacier, pur- 'forth' plus chacier 'to chase': to purchase was to go after something until you had it. Only in the mid-14c. did 'get by paying money' become the dominant sense.
senses.whyCN: 动词来自古法语 porchacier，由 pur-「向前」加 chacier「追逐」构成：purchase 本是「追着去取得」。到 14 世纪中期，「付钱取得」才成为主义。

senses.title: Procurement: the formal act of acquiring
senses.titleCN: 购置：有手续的正式取得
senses.definition: the formal or large-scale act of buying goods, equipment, or property
senses.definitionCN: 正式或大宗地购买货物、设备或财产的行为
senses.example: The university approved the purchase of new laboratory equipment.
senses.exampleCN: 校方批准了购置新的实验室设备。
senses.why: The noun's sense 'act of acquiring, procurement' is recorded from the late 14c. Modern institutions narrowed it to documented buying: the chase is gone, and what remains is a deliberate, recorded acquisition.
senses.whyCN: 名词「取得、采购的行为」记录于 14 世纪后期。现代机构把它收窄为有单据的购买：追逐不见了，剩下的是有步骤、有记录的取得。

senses.title: The thing bought: an object with a receipt
senses.titleCN: 购得之物：带小票的那件东西
senses.definition: something that has been bought
senses.definitionCN: 已经买到手的东西
senses.example: Her most expensive purchase was a second-hand piano.
senses.exampleCN: 她最贵的一件购得之物是一架二手钢琴。
senses.why: 'That which is bought' dates from the 1580s, three centuries after the verb. The older noun meant 'acquisition, booty'; once buying became the main sense, the object bought could inherit the name.
senses.whyCN: 「买到的东西」这一义项始于 16 世纪 80 年代，比动词晚三百年。早先名词指「获得物、战利品」；当购买成为主义，被买下的东西就继承了这个词。

senses.title: To win at a price: obtain by effort or loss
senses.titleCN: 以代价取得：用努力或牺牲换来
senses.definition: to obtain something valuable through effort, suffering, or sacrifice rather than money
senses.definitionCN: 通过努力、受苦或牺牲而得到有价值的东西，而非用钱
senses.example: They purchased their freedom with years of struggle.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用多年的斗争换来了自由。
senses.why: This is the oldest English sense: c.1300 purchase meant 'acquire, obtain, procure' by any means, including merit or suffering. 'To purchase peace with blood' keeps that breadth, where money is only one possible price.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语里最古老的义项：约 1300 年 purchase 指以任何方式「取得、获得、谋得」，包括功劳或受苦。「以鲜血换取和平」保留了这种宽度，钱只是众多代价之一。

senses.title: A firm grip: the hold that keeps the thing
senses.titleCN: 紧握：攥住不放的那只手
senses.definition: a firm hold or grasp on something, especially one that gives control
senses.definitionCN: 对某物的牢固抓握，尤指带来控制权的握持
senses.example: He got a purchase on the rope and pulled himself up.
senses.exampleCN: 他抓住绳子，把自己拉了上去。
senses.why: The noun sense 'firm hold by which power may be exerted' is from 1711, extended from a nautical verb of the 1560s meaning 'to haul or draw, especially by mechanical power', as sailors purchase an anchor. Gripping and buying share the image of pulling something into your possession.
senses.whyCN: 名词「可以施加力量的牢固把握」始于 1711 年，来自 16 世纪 60 年代一个航海动词「拉、绞（尤用机械力）」，如水手绞起锚。抓握与购买共享同一个意象：把东西拉进自己的掌控。

senses.title: Leverage: the point where a small force wins
senses.titleCN: 杠杆支点：小力撬动大物的那个点
senses.definition: a position or hold that gives mechanical advantage, the point where a lever or force bites
senses.definitionCN: 带来机械优势的位置或着力点，即杠杆或力量咬住的那一点
senses.example: Put the jack under the beam to get a better purchase.
senses.exampleCN: 把千斤顶放到梁下，好取得更好的着力点。
senses.why: Mechanical 'purchase' names the hold or position that lets a small force move a great weight, the same word sailors used for hauling. The point where the lever bites is literally a place to grip.
senses.whyCN: 机械上的 purchase 指让小力移动重物的着力点或握位，正是水手「绞拉」时用的词。杠杆咬住的那一点，字面上就是一个可以握紧的地方。

senses.title: Purchasing: buying turned into a department
senses.titleCN: 采购：变成一门部门工作的购买
senses.definition: the institutional activity or department responsible for buying supplies and equipment
senses.definitionCN: 负责购买物资与设备的机构性活动或部门
senses.example: She works in purchasing, sourcing parts for the whole factory.
senses.exampleCN: 她在采购部工作，为整个工厂寻找零件。
senses.why: In business and government, purchasing became a department and a process in the 20th c.: purchase orders, purchasing agents. The act of buying is institutionalised and separated from the person who pays.
senses.whyCN: 在商业与政府里，purchasing 在 20 世纪成为一个部门和流程：采购订单、采购员。购买行为被制度化，与掏钱的人分开了。

senses.title: To secure title: land and rights, not shopping
senses.titleCN: 置产、买断：买的是产权，不是商品
senses.definition: to acquire property, land, or legal rights by payment, especially on a large or formal scale
senses.definitionCN: 通过付款取得财产、土地或法律权利，尤指大宗或正式的
senses.example: The company purchased the land from the county in 1998.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司于 1998 年从县政府买下了这块土地。
senses.why: Legal and landed use keeps the noun's weight: a purchase of land or of rights is an acquisition of title, not a shopping trip. The word still carries the old sense of getting something permanently into your holdings.
senses.whyCN: 法律与地产用法保留了名词的分量：purchase of land or rights 是取得产权，而不是逛街购物。这个词仍带着「把某物永久纳入自己名下」的旧义。

senses.title: Booty: what was taken before it was bought
senses.titleCN: 掠夺所得：还没「买」之前，是抢来的
senses.definition: in older usage, goods gained by pillage or robbery; spoils
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法：通过掠夺或抢劫得到的财物；战利品
senses.example: In the old chronicle, the raiders divided their purchase among the ships.
senses.exampleCN: 在那部旧编年史里，劫掠者把抢来的财物分给了各条船。
senses.why: The noun's first English sense (c.1300) was 'booty, spoil, goods gained by pillage'; 'to make purchase' once meant 'to seize by robbery'. The polite buyer of today stands where a raider once stood.
senses.whyCN: 名词最早的英语义项（约 1300 年）是「战利品、掠夺所得」；to make purchase 一度意为「抢劫夺取」。今天彬彬有礼的买主，站的是当年劫掠者的位置。

intro.en: Purchase begins as a chase, not a transaction: Old French porchacier meant to go after something and get it. Money entered the word only in the 14th century, and the grip-and-lever senses came from sailors hauling anchors.
intro.cn: purchase 起于追逐而非交易：古法语 porchacier 意为追着去取得。金钱在 14 世纪才进入这个词，而「抓握、杠杆」义来自水手绞锚。

items.en: Porchacier (later pourchasser) meant 'search for, procure; aim at, strive for, pursue eagerly'. It joins pur- 'forth' with chacier 'to run after, hunt, chase' (see chase). The exact force of pur- here, whether 'forward' or an intensive, is uncertain and is marked source uncertain.
items.cn: Porchacier（后作 pourchasser）意为「寻找、谋得、力求、急切追求」，由 pur-「向前」加 chacier「追赶、打猎、追逐」（见 chase）构成。pur- 在此究竟是「向前」还是加强语气，来源不确定，故标为「来源不确定」。

items.en: The Anglo-French verb purchaser meant 'go after' and carried the legal-administrative tone of obtaining something. English took it over as purchase with a very wide meaning.
items.cn: 盎格鲁-法语动词 purchaser 意为「追赶、追求」，并带有取得某物的法律行政语气。英语借用为 purchase，含义非常宽。

items.en: The verb is first recorded as 'acquire, obtain; get, receive; procure, provide', also 'bring about, instigate, contrive'. At this stage money is not required: merit, suffering, or effort can be the price.
items.cn: 动词最早记录为「取得、获得、得到、领受、谋得、提供」，也有「促成、煽动、策划」义。此时并不需要金钱：功劳、受苦或努力都可以是代价。

items.en: The specific sense 'acquire or secure by expenditure of money or its equivalent, pay money for, buy' appears in the mid-14c. The older 'get by conquest in war, obtain as booty' survived into the 17c.
items.cn: 「以金钱或其等价物取得、付钱买下」这一具体义项出现于 14 世纪中期。更早的「以战争征服取得、作为战利品获得」一直用到 17 世纪。

items.en: A nautical verb 'to haul or draw, especially by mechanical power' (1560s, used of hauling up anchors) produced the noun sense 'firm hold by which power may be exerted' in 1711. Meanwhile 'that which is bought' is recorded from the 1580s.
items.cn: 航海动词「拉、绞，尤指用机械力」（16 世纪 60 年代，用于绞起锚）在 1711 年衍生出名词「可以施加力量的牢固把握」；同时「买到的东西」记录于 16 世纪 80 年代。

items.en: The noun's journey runs from 'booty, spoil' (c.1300) to 'act of acquiring' (late 14c.) to 'thing bought' (1580s) and finally to the 20th-century department of purchasing. Plunder, transaction, object, institution: one word, four stages.
items.cn: 名词的旅程从「战利品、掠夺物」（约 1300）到「取得行为」（14 世纪后期），再到「买到的东西」（16 世纪 80 年代），最后到 20 世纪的采购部门。劫掠、交易、物品、机构：一个词，四个阶段。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写和读音挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: to follow or chase someone, or to work toward a goal. It echoes purchase in sound but comes from Latin prosequi, not from chacier.
entries.definitionCN: 追赶；追求。它与 purchase 读音相近，但来自拉丁语 prosequi，而非 chacier。

entries.definition: the act of chasing or striving for something. Like pursue, it belongs to the sequi 'follow' family.
entries.definitionCN: 追赶；追求。与 pursue 一样属于 sequi「跟随」词族。

entries.definition: to read through carefully. It looks like purchase but has no etymological link.
entries.definitionCN: 细读；浏览。它形似 purchase，但词源上毫无关联。

entries.definition: an aim or intention. It also begins with pur-, but the second element is poser 'to place'.
entries.definitionCN: 目的；意图。它同样以 pur- 开头，但后半是 poser「放置」。

entries.definition: to get something by paying money. It is the short native verb where purchase is the formal one.
entries.definitionCN: 买。它是简短的本族动词，purchase 则是正式用词。

entries.definition: to come to possess something, often through effort or over time, not necessarily by payment.
entries.definitionCN: 获得；取得。常指通过努力或随时间而拥有，不一定付钱。

entries.definition: to obtain something, especially with care or difficulty. It matches the oldest sense of purchase.
entries.definitionCN: 设法取得，尤指费心或费力地。它对应 purchase 最古老的义项。

entries.definition: to get something, especially by request or effort. Neutral in tone, wider than buy.
entries.definitionCN: 获得。尤指通过请求或努力，语气中性，比 buy 宽。

entries.definition: a firm hold on something. It covers the physical sense of purchase as grip or leverage.
entries.definitionCN: 紧握；抓握。它对应 purchase 表示抓握或着力点的实指义。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Old French chacier 'to chase', Anglo-French purchaser, and the nautical hauling sense that gave us the grip.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：古法语 chacier「追逐」、盎格鲁-法语 purchaser，以及带来「抓握」义的航海绞拉用法。

normal.en: purchase = pur- 'forward' + chase: you chase something forward until it is yours.
normal.cn: purchase = pur-「向前」+ chase「追」：你一路往前追，直到它归你所有。

normal.en: The same chase lives in catch and capture: to purchase is to run something down and seize it.
normal.cn: 同一个 chase 也活在 catch 和 capture 里：purchase 就是把东西追到手并抓住。

normal.en: Sailors purchase an anchor by hauling it up; that is why a good foothold is also called a purchase.
normal.cn: 水手用绞拉的方式 purchase（绞起）锚；所以一个稳的落脚点也叫 purchase（着力点）。

normal.en: A purchaser is simply the person at the end of the chase, holding the receipt.
normal.cn: purchaser 不过是追逐终点的那个拿着小票的人。

normal.en: To purchase peace with blood is the word's oldest logic: the price need not be money.
normal.cn: 以鲜血 purchase 和平，是这个词最古老的逻辑：代价不必是钱。

abstract.en: The core is possession by pursuit: first you chase, then you hold, and only later do you pay.
abstract.cn: 核心是「追而得之」：先追、再抓，最后才付钱。

abstract.en: Money is a late guest in this word, not its host.
abstract.cn: 金钱在这个词里是迟到的客人，而不是主人。

abstract.en: Purchase keeps a raider and a shopper in one body: booty, then bargain.
abstract.cn: purchase 把劫掠者和购物者装在同一个身体里：先是战利品，后是讨价还价。

examples.en: The city purchased the old railway yard and turned it into a park.
examples.cn: 市政府买下了旧铁路场，把它改造成了公园。

examples.en: Keep your receipt as proof of purchase in case the radio fails.
examples.cn: 留好小票作为购买凭证，以防收音机出故障。

examples.en: The climber finally got a purchase on the rock and pulled himself over the edge.
examples.cn: 攀登者终于抓牢了岩壁，把自己拉上了边缘。

dict_mnemonic.text: pur（向前）+ chase（追）——追上去一把抓住，后来才变成「花钱买下」→ purchase 购买

root: 源自拉丁语系：古法语 porchacier（pur-「向前」+ chacier「追逐」，同 chase）经盎格鲁-法语 purchaser 进入英语，本义「追着取得」，14 世纪中期才特化为「用钱买」；「抓握、着力点」义另出自 16 世纪水手绞锚的航海动词。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one arc: chase, seize, pay, own. The verb starts as 'get by going after', narrows to 'buy', then splits into the object bought, the grip that holds it, the lever point that moves it, and the institution that orders it.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿着一条弧线：追、抓、付、拥有。动词从「追着取得」开始，收窄为「买」，再分出「买到的东西」「攥住它的手」「撬动它的支点」以及「下订单的机构」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: chasing something down and closing your hand around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：追着一样东西跑，最后把它攥进手心。

branches.en: THE TRANSACTION: ordinary buying, and the formal act of procurement.
branches.cn: 交易：日常购买，以及正式的购置行为。

branches.en: WHAT IS TAKEN: the thing bought, and the old booty seized by force.
branches.cn: 被取走之物：买到的东西，以及旧时武力夺来的战利品。

branches.en: GETTING BY OTHER MEANS: winning through sacrifice, and securing property by title.
branches.cn: 以别的代价取得：用牺牲换来，以及以产权买断。

branches.en: THE GRIP: a firm hold, and the point where a lever bites.
branches.cn: 抓握：牢固的握持，以及杠杆咬住的着力点。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION: purchasing as a department, an order, a process.
branches.cn: 机构：作为部门、订单与流程的采购。

intro.en: Purchase is pur- plus chacier plus the English noun ending. Its family shows the prefix pur- 'forth', the root chac-/capt- 'to chase, seize', and the suffixes -er, -ing, -able, and re-.
intro.cn: purchase 是 pur- 加 chacier，再加英语名词词尾。它的词族展示前缀 pur-「向前」、词根 chac-/capt-「追逐、抓取」，以及后缀 -er、-ing、-able 和 re-。

latinIntro.en: Behind chacier stands Vulgar Latin captiare and Latin captare 'to try to catch', from capere 'to take'. The same capere yields capture, captive and catch, so buying and seizing are cousins.
latinIntro.cn: chacier 背后是通俗拉丁语 captiare 与拉丁语 captare「设法抓住」，源自 capere「拿取」。同一个 capere 还给出 capture、captive、catch，因此「买」与「抓」是表亲。

items.meaning: to obtain by chasing, then by paying
items.example: They purchased the house in cash.
items.exampleCN: 他们用现金买下了这栋房子。

items.meaningCN: 购买者；买主（-er 施事后缀）
items.example: The purchaser must be over eighteen.
items.exampleCN: 购买者必须年满十八岁。

items.meaning: the act or department of buying
to buy back or buy again
items.example: The firm repurchased two million shares.
items.exampleCN: 该公司回购了两百万股。

items.meaningCN: 可购得的（-able 形容词后缀）

items.meaning: to run after in order to catch
items.meaningCN: 追逐；追赶（purchase 的后半身）
items.example: The dog chased the ball across the lawn.

items.meaningCN: 抓住；接住（chase 的同源双式词）
items.example: He caught the falling cup just in time.
items.exampleCN: 他及时接住了掉下来的杯子。

items.meaning: to take by force; the act of taking
items.meaningCN: 俘获；夺取（capere 的另一支后裔）
items.example: The soldiers captured the bridge at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 士兵们在黎明夺取了那座桥。

items.example: The unpurchased land stayed wild for decades.
items.exampleCN: 那块未被买下的土地荒了几十年。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 追赶；打猎（chacier 的直接来源）

definition_zh: 纯的；不掺杂的；纯粹的；纯理论的；纯洁的
definition_en: containing nothing except the stated substance, being nothing more than what is said, or studied without thought of practical use
core_image: 一只玻璃杯里的水清到能看见杯底纹路，旁边一滴墨也没落进去
scene: 实验台上摆着一只玻璃杯，里面的水清得能看见杯底的纹路，桌边连一滴墨水也没有。The lab uses only pure water for this test, because any impurity would change the result.
sceneCN: 这里取「纯的、不掺杂的」（第 1 个义项：只含有所说的物质，没有杂质）；句意为实验室这项测试只用纯水，因为任何杂质都会改变结果。能看见杯底纹路的清水就是线索。

pos.zh: 纯的；不掺杂的；纯粹的；纯理论的；纯洁的

derivatives.zh: 由 pure 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「纯净；纯度」
由拉丁词干 pur- 加 -ify（源自 facere，做）构成，义为「净化；提纯」
由 pure 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「纯粹地；仅仅」
由 purify 加 -cation 构成，义为「净化；提纯」

senses.title: Not mixed with anything else
senses.definition: containing nothing except the stated substance, with no added or foreign matter
senses.definitionCN: 只含有所说的那种物质，没有添加物或外来杂质
senses.example: The spring behind the house still gives pure water.
senses.exampleCN: 屋后的泉水至今仍出清水。
senses.why: Latin purus described something clean and unmixed, so the word begins with a physical test: what is left when everything foreign has been taken out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 purus 指干净、不混杂的东西，所以这个词的起点是一次很具体的检验：把一切外来的东西去掉之后还剩下什么。

senses.title: Nothing more than what is stated
senses.definition: used to stress that something is only what it is said to be, with nothing else added
senses.definitionCN: 用来强调某事只是所说的那样，没有别的成分
senses.example: Winning the prize was pure luck, since he had entered at the last minute.
senses.exampleCN: 得奖纯属运气，因为他是最后一刻才报名的。
senses.why: Once no foreign substance is allowed in, the word can also refuse any hidden cause: pure luck means luck with nothing else mixed in, not even effort.
senses.whyCN: 一旦不允许掺入外来物质，这个词也能用来排除任何隐藏的原因：pure luck 就是运气里不掺别的东西，连努力都不算。

senses.title: Studied without a practical aim
senses.definition: of a subject or a study, done to understand it rather than to use it for a practical purpose
senses.definitionCN: 指学科或研究出于理解本身而做，而不是为了实际用途
senses.example: She chose pure mathematics over engineering because she liked proofs more than machines.
senses.exampleCN: 她选了纯数学而不是工程，因为她喜欢证明胜过机器。
senses.why: A pure science is separated from application the way pure water is separated from everything dissolved in it: the practical part has been filtered out.
senses.whyCN: 纯科学与应用分开，正如纯水与溶于其中的一切分开：实用的部分被滤掉了，剩下的是学科本身。

senses.title: Morally clean and innocent
senses.definition: free from evil or sexual suggestion, often used of a person, a heart or a motive
senses.definitionCN: 没有邪恶或色情意味的，常用于形容人、心灵或动机
senses.example: Her motives were pure, and nobody could accuse her of seeking money.
senses.exampleCN: 她的动机是纯洁的，谁也不能指责她图钱。
senses.why: The Latin word for physically clean slid into the moral field early, because a stain that can be washed off is an easy picture for guilt that can be removed.
senses.whyCN: 那个表示「物理上干净」的拉丁词很早就滑入道德领域，因为「能洗掉的污渍」是「能去除的罪责」现成的画面。

intro.en: Pure comes from Latin purus, clean and unmixed; Old French reshaped it before English took it, and the moral sense arrived early.
intro.cn: pure 来自拉丁语 purus（干净、不混杂）；古法语先把它改造过，随后英语借入，道德义很早就一并带了过来。

items.en: Purus meant clean and free from mixture; its deeper origin is uncertain, and a common guess links it to an old root for cleansing.
items.cn: purus 意为干净、不混杂；它更早的来源不确定，一般认为与一个表示「清洗」的古老词根有关。

items.en: Purus combined with facere, to make, giving purificare, to make clean, the source of purify and purification.
items.cn: purus 与 facere（做、使）结合成 purificare（使干净），是 purify 与 purification 的来源。

items.en: Old French kept pur for clean and unmixed and also used it for what is morally blameless.
items.cn: 古法语用 pur 表示干净、不混杂，也用它指道德上没有过失的。

items.en: Middle English pure carried both the physical and the moral sense and added the sense of nothing but.
items.cn: 中古英语的 pure 同时带着物理义与道德义，并加入了「只不过是」的意思。

items.en: Modern English spreads the word across water, motives, luck and mathematics, all of them versions of nothing added.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词分摊到水、动机、运气和数学上，而这些全都是「没有添加」的不同版本。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin adjective for clean; the near-meaning group gathers words for being free of mixture or of any other cause.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「干净」形容词上的词；近义组收表示不含杂质或不受其他原因影响的词。

entries.definition: The state of being pure.
entries.definitionCN: 纯净的状态；纯度。

entries.definition: To remove what is not wanted from something.
entries.definitionCN: 除去某物中不需要的成分。

entries.definition: Someone who insists on the exact original standards of a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 坚持某领域原有纯正标准的人。

entries.definition: To claim to be or to mean something; the spelling is close, but this word comes from a different Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 声称是或意指某事；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Free from dirt or unwanted matter.
entries.definitionCN: 没有污垢或多余东西的。

entries.definition: Used to stress that something is nothing but what is named.
entries.definitionCN: 用来强调某事只是所说的那样。

entries.definition: Not combined with anything else.
entries.definitionCN: 没有与其他东西混合的。

entries.definition: Complete, with nothing added or limiting.
entries.definitionCN: 完全的，没有任何附加或限制的。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin adjective for clean and unmixed, and its family keeps moving outward from water to motives, to theory and to blame.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「干净、不混杂」的形容词上，同族词从水一路向动机、理论和过失扩展。

normal.en: Purus means clean and unmixed, so pure is a word about what has been removed as much as about what is there.
normal.cn: purus 意为干净、不混杂，所以 pure 既在说剩下的东西，也在说被去掉的东西。

normal.en: Purity adds -ity and names the state; purify adds -ify and names the act of making something clean.
normal.cn: purity 加 -ity 指状态，purify 加 -ify 指使某物变干净的动作。

normal.en: Pure science is not a science washed with water; it is study with the practical aim filtered out, the same picture applied to ideas.
normal.cn: pure science 不是用水洗过的科学，而是把实用目的滤掉的研究，是同一个画面用在观念上。

normal.en: Pure luck and pure gold use the same logic: nothing else is mixed in, whether the thing is metal or chance.
normal.cn: pure luck 与 pure gold 逻辑相同：不管那是金属还是运气，里面都没有掺别的东西。

normal.en: The moral sense is old, not modern: a stain that can be washed away has long been a picture for guilt that can be removed.
normal.cn: 道德义并不新：能洗掉的污渍，很久以来就是「能去除的罪责」的画面。

abstract.en: To call something pure is to make a claim about its edges: nothing outside has got in.
abstract.cn: 说某物纯，其实是在为它的边界作证：外面的东西没有进来。

abstract.en: A pure motive and a pure metal are judged by the same question, namely what else is present.
abstract.cn: 纯动机与纯金属要用同一个问题来判断，那就是里面还有什么别的东西。

abstract.en: The word keeps reminding us that purity is defined by absence, not by addition.
abstract.cn: 这个词一直提醒人：纯是由「没有什么」来定义的，而不是由「多了什么」。

examples.en: The spring behind the house still gives pure water.
examples.cn: 屋后的泉水至今仍出清水。

examples.en: Winning the prize was pure luck, since he had entered at the last minute.
examples.cn: 得奖纯属运气，因为他是最后一刻才报名的。

examples.en: She chose pure mathematics over engineering because she liked proofs more than machines.
examples.cn: 她选了纯数学而不是工程，因为她喜欢证明胜过机器。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读音近「漂尔」——衣服漂洗到只剩清水，一点泡沫都没有，就是 pure。

root: 拉丁语 purus（干净、不混杂），其更早来源不确定，一般认为与表示「清洗」的词根有关；经古法语 pur 进入英语。同族的 purity、purify 都出自 purus。

sensesIntro.en: The core is nothing foreign inside; the senses divide into a substance without mixture, a statement with nothing behind it, study without use, and a person without blame.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「里面没有外来的东西」；义项分成不掺杂的物质、背后别无他物的说法、不为实用的研究，以及没有过失的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glass of water so clear that the pattern on its bottom shows through, with not one drop of ink nearby.
core.cn: 核心意象：一杯清到能看见杯底纹路的水，旁边一滴墨也没有。

branches.en: a glass of water clear down to the etched bottom
branches.cn: 一杯清到能看见杯底纹路的水

branches.en: a prize won on a ticket bought at the last minute
branches.cn: 最后一刻买票却中了奖

branches.en: a blackboard covered with a proof and no diagram
branches.cn: 写满证明、没画一张图的黑板

branches.en: a hand raised to swear that no money was wanted
branches.cn: 举手发誓不为钱的那只手

branches.en: a cup holding nothing but water and nothing else
branches.cn: 杯子里除了水什么都没有

intro.en: A Latin adjective for clean holds the word together, and Latin and English endings build the nouns of state and the verb of making clean.
intro.cn: 表示「干净」的拉丁语形容词支撑着这个词，拉丁语与英语的词尾再构成表示状态的名词和表示「使之干净」的动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin purus, clean and unmixed, the noun puritas, and the verb purificare are the direct sources of the English word and its relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 purus（干净、不混杂）、名词 puritas 与动词 purificare 是英语这个词及其同族词的直接来源。

definition_zh: 仅仅；完全；纯粹地；纯洁地
definition_en: only, completely, and for no other reason or purpose than the one that is stated
core_image: 一张空桌上只放着一支笔，别的什么都没有
scene: 排练结束后，有人问那位老人为什么每周都来帮忙，他摆摆手，说自己只是喜欢听孩子们唱歌。He came purely out of curiosity, with no plan to buy anything.
sceneCN: 这里取「仅仅、完全」（第 1 个义项：所说原因是唯一涉及的原因）；句意是他来纯粹出于好奇，并没有买东西的打算。老人摆手不收报酬的动作就是线索。

pos.zh: 仅仅；完全；纯粹地；纯洁地

derivatives.zh: purely 的词基，去掉副词词尾 -ly 即得，义为「纯的；纯粹的」
由 pure 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「纯净；纯度」
由拉丁词干 pur- 加 -ify 构成，义为「净化；提纯」

senses.title: Only, and nothing else
senses.definition: used to show that the reason or quality just named is the only one involved
senses.definitionCN: 用来表明刚才所说的原因或性质是唯一涉及的
senses.example: The meeting was called purely to explain the new rules.
senses.exampleCN: 召开这次会议只是为了解释新规定。
senses.why: The -ly ending turns the adjective into a lens: whatever follows is seen as nothing but itself, with every other motive removed.
senses.whyCN: -ly 把形容词变成一面透镜：后面跟的东西只被看成它本身，其他动机全被剔除。

senses.title: For no other purpose than the one named
senses.definition: done only for the reason given, with no hidden or practical aim
senses.definitionCN: 只因为所说的理由而做，没有隐藏的或实际的目的
senses.example: She joined the choir purely for the pleasure of singing.
senses.exampleCN: 她加入合唱团纯粹是为了唱歌的乐趣。
senses.why: This is the first sense applied to a motive: when one purpose is named alone, the word quietly denies that money, fame or duty played any part.
senses.whyCN: 这是第一个义项用在动机上：当只点出一个目的时，这个词就在悄悄否认金钱、名声或义务起过作用。

senses.title: In theory rather than in practice
senses.definition: considered as an idea or a model, without being tested in real conditions
senses.definitionCN: 作为观念或模型来考虑，未在真实条件下检验
senses.example: Purely theoretically, the bridge could hold twice that weight.
senses.exampleCN: 纯从理论上说，那座桥能承受两倍的重量。
senses.why: A pure substance has nothing foreign in it, and a purely theoretical question has no case, no data and no site mixed into it.
senses.whyCN: 纯物质里没有外来成分，纯理论问题里也不掺具体案例、数据和现场，两者的结构是一样的。

senses.title: In a clean or blameless way
senses.definition: in a manner free from wrongdoing, used mostly of living or behaving
senses.definitionCN: 以没有过失的方式，多用于形容生活或行为
senses.example: He lived purely and gave away most of what he earned.
senses.exampleCN: 他生活清白，把挣来的大部分都捐了出去。
senses.why: The moral branch of pure reaches the adverb here: to act purely is to act with nothing soiled in the intention.
senses.whyCN: pure 的道德分支在这里落到副词上：purely 地做事，就是意图里没有任何被弄脏的部分。

intro.en: Purely is the English adverb built on pure, which came from Latin purus through Old French; its ending is the native English -ly.
intro.cn: purely 是由 pure 构成的英语副词，而 pure 经古法语来自拉丁语 purus；它的词尾是英语本土的 -ly。

items.en: Purus meant clean and unmixed, and it is the source of the whole English family.
items.cn: purus 意为干净、不混杂，是英语这一族词的源头。

items.en: Old French kept pur for clean and unmixed and also for what is morally blameless, and English borrowed the adjective from it.
items.cn: 古法语用 pur 表示干净、不混杂，也指道德上没有过失的；英语从这个形容词借入。

items.en: Middle English pure named what is free of mixture, and the adverb was then built on it inside English.
items.cn: 中古英语的 pure 指没有混杂的东西，副词随后在英语内部由它构成。

items.en: The adverbial ending came from Old English -lice, which became -ly and turns an adjective into a word about manner.
items.cn: 副词词尾来自古英语 -lice，后来写作 -ly，把形容词变成描述方式的一类词。

items.en: Modern English uses purely mostly as a limiter, telling the listener that nothing else stands behind what was said.
items.cn: 现代英语中的 purely 多半起限定作用，告诉听者所说的事情背后没有别的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the adjective that stands behind the adverb and its closest relatives; the near-meaning group gathers other adverbs of limitation.
note.cn: 形近组收这个副词背后的形容词及其最近的同族词；近义组收其他表示限定的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective from which this adverb is built.
entries.definitionCN: 构成这个副词的原形容词。

entries.definition: The quality of being pure.
entries.definitionCN: 纯净的性质；纯度。

entries.definition: To make something clean by removing what is unwanted.
entries.definitionCN: 除去不需要的成分使某物变干净。

entries.definition: A person who keeps strictly to the original standards of a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 严格坚持某领域原有标准的人。

entries.definition: Only, and nothing more.
entries.definitionCN: 仅仅，不过。

entries.definition: For one reason only, or in a plain way.
entries.definitionCN: 仅仅；简单地。

entries.definition: For that one reason and no other.
entries.definitionCN: 仅仅；唯一地。

normalIntro.en: The word is the adjective for clean lifted into an adverb of narrowing, and its memories sit on the -ly ending and on the idea of one cause only.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是把表示「干净」的形容词抬升为起收窄作用的副词，记忆点落在 -ly 词尾和「只有一个原因」上。

normal.en: Purely is pure plus -ly, so it does to the adjective what quickly does to quick.
normal.cn: purely 是 pure 加 -ly，它对形容词做的事，和 quickly 对 quick 做的一样。

normal.en: The -ly ending came from Old English -lice and has always answered the question of how.
normal.cn: -ly 词尾来自古英语 -lice，一直用来回答「怎样」这个问题。

normal.en: Purely by chance removes human intention from the sentence, leaving only chance in the frame.
normal.cn: purely by chance 把人的意图从句子中拿掉，画面里只剩「偶然」。

normal.en: Purely theoretical is the adverb version of pure science: the practical part has been filtered out.
normal.cn: purely theoretical 是 pure science 的副词版：实用的部分已经被滤掉。

normal.en: The moral use, as in living purely, is the oldest layer of purus still visible in an everyday adverb.
normal.cn: 表示道德义的 living purely，是 purus 最古老的一层仍留在日常副词里的痕迹。

abstract.en: An adverb of purity works like a spotlight: it darkens everything except the one thing named.
abstract.cn: 表示纯粹的副词像一盏聚光灯：除了被点到的那样东西，其余全被压暗。

abstract.en: Saying purely is a way of closing doors, one by one, until only one reason is left in the room.
abstract.cn: 说 purely 就是把门一扇扇关上，直到屋里只剩一个理由。

abstract.en: The word is small but it carries a whole claim about cause, which is why it so often ends an argument.
abstract.cn: 这个词很小，却包含了一整套关于因果的主张，所以它常常能给争论画上句号。

examples.en: The meeting was called purely to explain the new rules.
examples.cn: 召开这次会议只是为了解释新规定。

examples.en: She joined the choir purely for the pleasure of singing.
examples.cn: 她加入合唱团纯粹是为了唱歌的乐趣。

examples.en: He came purely out of curiosity, with no plan to buy anything.
examples.cn: 他来纯粹出于好奇，并没有买东西的打算。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读音近「漂离」——把别的东西都漂洗掉，只剩下本身，就是纯粹地。

root: 拉丁语 purus（干净、不混杂）经古法语 pur 进入英语作 pure，再加古英语副词词尾 -lice（今 -ly）构成 purely。

sensesIntro.en: The core is one thing with nothing behind it; the senses divide into a single reason, a single purpose, theory without practice, and a blameless life.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「只有这一样，背后别无他物」；义项分成唯一的原因、唯一的目的、脱离实践的理论，以及没有过失的生活。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single pen left on an otherwise empty desk.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张空桌上只放着一支笔。

branches.en: a single pen left on an otherwise empty desk
branches.cn: 空桌上只留一支笔

branches.en: a man waving away payment for his help
branches.cn: 老人摆手不收报酬

branches.en: a calculation done on paper and never built
branches.cn: 只在纸上算过、从未建造

branches.en: a life with nothing hidden in it
branches.cn: 没有隐藏之事的一生

branches.en: a word that narrows a sentence down to one cause
branches.cn: 把整句话收窄到唯一原因的一个词

intro.en: A Latin adjective for clean and a native English adverb ending hold the word together, and the same stem also grows nouns and a verb.
intro.cn: 表示「干净」的拉丁语形容词与英语本土副词词尾共同支撑这个词，同一词干还长出名词与动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin purus, clean and unmixed, and the noun puritas stand behind the adjective, and English added the adverbial ending -ly to form this word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 purus（干净、不混杂）与名词 puritas 是那个形容词的来源，英语再加副词词尾 -ly 构成了这个词。

items.meaning: one who insists on pure standards

definition_zh: 紫色的；紫色；紫袍；尊贵地位；辞藻华丽的
definition_en: of the colour between red and blue, or that colour itself, also used for the robe of high rank and for writing that is too showy
core_image: 一点紫红染料落进清水，颜色一缕缕散开
scene: 染坊里，工匠从陶罐里刮出一点深红的粉末，放进水里，颜色立刻一缕缕散开。The robe was dyed a deep purple that only the richest families could afford.
sceneCN: 这里取「紫色（颜色本身）」（第 2 个义项：介于红与蓝之间的颜色，尤指深色）；句意为那件袍子染成深紫色，只有最富的人家才付得起。陶罐里刮出的染料粉末就是线索。

pos.zh: 紫色的；辞藻华丽的
紫色；紫袍；尊贵地位

derivatives.zh: 由 purple 加表示「略似……」的后缀 -ish 构成，义为「略带紫色的」
由 purple 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「偏紫的」
由 purple 与 heart 复合而成，指一种切开后呈紫色的热带木材

senses.title: Of the colour between red and blue
senses.definition: having the colour made by mixing red and blue, often in a deep shade
senses.definitionCN: 具有红蓝相混而成的颜色，常为较深的一种色调
senses.example: She wore a purple scarf that matched her gloves.
senses.exampleCN: 她系着一条紫色的围巾，和手套正好相配。
senses.why: The colour began as the name of a dye squeezed from a sea snail, so the adjective first named not a hue but the costly substance that produced it.
senses.whyCN: 这种颜色最初是一种从海螺里挤出的染料的名字，所以这个形容词最早说的不是色调，而是产生这个色调的昂贵材料。

senses.title: The colour itself
senses.definition: the colour lying between red and blue, especially the dark shade once made from shellfish
senses.definitionCN: 介于红与蓝之间的颜色，尤指从前由贝类制成的深色
senses.example: The walls were painted in a purple that looked almost black at night.
senses.exampleCN: 墙刷成一种紫色，夜里看上去几乎像黑色。
senses.why: Once the dye became a colour word, the name could stand alone as a noun, with no cloth or object attached to it.
senses.whyCN: 当染料名变成颜色词之后，这个名字就能单独作名词使用，不再依附于布或某件物品。

senses.title: Cloth or rank of the highest order
senses.definition: the purple robe of an emperor or a high official, and by extension the rank it stands for
senses.definitionCN: 皇帝或高官所穿的紫色袍服，引申指它所代表的尊贵地位
senses.example: He was born to the purple and never had to ask for a title.
senses.exampleCN: 他出身王室，从不需要去讨一个头衔。
senses.why: Because the dye was so expensive, purple cloth marked the few who could pay for it, and the garment became a shorthand for the rank itself.
senses.whyCN: 这种染料极其昂贵，所以紫布成了少数付得起的人的标志，衣袍本身便成了地位的代称。

senses.title: Writing that is too showy
senses.titleCN: 辞藻华丽的；华而不实的
senses.definition: of writing, full of ornate words and effects, often far too many of them
senses.definitionCN: 指文字堆砌华美词句与效果，常嫌过分
senses.example: The young critic called the novel purple, all decoration and no plot.
senses.exampleCN: 那位年轻评论家说这部小说辞藻浮艳，全是装点，没有情节。
senses.why: Purple cloth was the most decorated thing a rich person could wear, so the same word attaches to prose that is dressed up far beyond its content.
senses.whyCN: 紫布是富人身上最能装点的东西，于是同一个词也用在打扮得远超其内容的文字上。

intro.en: Purple names a dye taken from a sea snail; the word travelled from Greek through Latin and Old English, and its Greek starting point is itself of uncertain origin.
intro.cn: purple 原是一种取自海螺的染料之名；这个词从希腊语经拉丁语、古英语一路传来，而它的希腊语起点本身来源不确定。

items.en: Porphyra named the murex shellfish and the crimson dye taken from it; the Greek word is often said to come from a Semitic source, so its origin is not certain.
items.cn: porphyra 指骨螺这种贝类以及从中取得的深红染料；这个词一般认为来自闪米特语，来源不确定。

items.en: Latin borrowed it as purpura and used it for the dye, the colour and the costly cloth.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入作 purpura，用来指染料、颜色与昂贵的织物。

items.en: The verb purpurare meant to dye something purple, a sign of how tightly the colour was tied to a craft and a trade.
items.cn: 动词 purpurare 意为「染成紫色」，这说明这种颜色与一门手艺、一桩买卖绑得很紧。

items.en: Old English borrowed the word early as purpul, probably straight from Latin rather than through French, and used it for the colour and for cloth.
items.cn: 古英语很早就借入这个词，写作 purpul，可能直接来自拉丁语而非经由法语，用来指颜色和织物。

items.en: Modern English settled the spelling as purple and kept the older senses of rank and of showy writing beside the everyday colour word.
items.cn: 现代英语把拼写固定为 purple，并在日常颜色义之外保留了「尊位」与「浮艳文字」两层旧义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Greek and Latin names for the dye; the near-meaning group gathers the neighbouring colour names.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在希腊语与拉丁语染料名上的词；近义组收相邻的颜色名称。

entries.definition: Slightly purple in colour.
entries.definitionCN: 颜色略带紫色的。

entries.definition: A hard rock with purple-red crystals set in it.
entries.definitionCN: 含紫红色斑晶的坚硬岩石。

entries.definition: A medical term for purple spots on the skin, taken from the Latin colour word.
entries.definitionCN: 医学上指皮肤上的紫斑，取自拉丁语的颜色词。

entries.definition: A tropical wood that turns purple when it is cut.
entries.definitionCN: 一种切开后呈紫色的热带木材。

entries.definition: A bluish-purple colour, or a small spring flower.
entries.definitionCN: 偏蓝的紫色，或一种春季小花。

entries.definition: A strong purplish red.
entries.definitionCN: 浓烈的紫红色。

entries.definition: A pale purple colour, or the bush with fragrant flowers.
entries.definitionCN: 淡紫色，或开香花的丁香丛。

entries.definition: A deep blue-purple colour obtained from a plant dye.
entries.definitionCN: 从植物染料取得的深蓝紫色。

normalIntro.en: The word is a dye before it is a colour, and its family keeps the sea snail, the costly cloth and the rank that cloth announced.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词先是染料名，然后才是颜色名；同族词一直保留着海螺、昂贵的紫布，以及紫布所宣告的地位。

normal.en: Greek porphyra named both the murex snail and the dye from it, so purple began as a substance rather than as a hue.
normal.cn: 希腊语 porphyra 同时指骨螺和它产出的染料，所以 purple 的起点是一种物质，而不是一种色调。

normal.en: Latin purpura kept dye, colour and cloth together, which is why one English word can still mean all three.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 purpura 把染料、颜色和布匹放在一起，所以一个英语词至今仍能同时指这三样。

normal.en: Purplish adds -ish, the suffix of likeness, so it means only somewhat purple rather than fully purple.
normal.cn: purplish 加 -ish 这个表示「相似」的后缀，所以它只表示「有点紫」，而不是完全的紫。

normal.en: Born to the purple is a phrase about rank, not about a birth in a violet room; the purple here is the robe.
normal.cn: born to the purple 说的是地位，不是生在紫色的房间里；这里的 purple 指那件袍子。

normal.en: Purple prose is writing dressed in its best clothes, and the judgement in the phrase comes from the old cost of the dye.
normal.cn: purple prose 指穿得过分讲究的文字，这个说法里的贬义来自染料昔日的高价。

abstract.en: A colour that once cost more than gold still carries rank whenever it is used of cloth.
abstract.cn: 这种颜色曾经比黄金还贵，所以它一用在布上，就仍然带着等级。

abstract.en: The same word can praise a robe and mock a sentence, because both are judged by how much they display.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能夸一件袍子，也能讥讽一个句子，因为两者都按「展示了多少」来评判。

abstract.en: Purple is a reminder that colours are never only colours; they arrive with a history of who could afford them.
abstract.cn: purple 提醒人：颜色从来不只是颜色，它随身带着「谁买得起」的历史。

examples.en: She wore a purple scarf that matched her gloves.
examples.cn: 她系着一条紫色的围巾，和手套正好相配。

examples.en: He was born to the purple and never had to ask for a title.
examples.cn: 他出身王室，从不需要去讨一个头衔。

examples.en: The walls were painted in a purple that looked almost black at night.
examples.cn: 墙刷成一种紫色，夜里看上去几乎像黑色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读音近「婆婆」——紫色是婆婆那件压箱底的缎子袄的颜色。

root: 希腊语 porphyra（骨螺及其深红染料，来源不确定）→ 拉丁语 purpura → 古英语 purpul → 现代英语 purple；同族的 porphyry 保留了希腊词形。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a dye more costly than the cloth it coloured; the senses divide into the hue, the colour as a noun, the robe and rank, and writing dressed too richly.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一种比它所染的布还贵的染料；义项分成色调、颜色本身、紫袍与地位，以及打扮得过分的文字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop of purple-red dye falling into clear water and opening in threads of colour.
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴紫红染料落进清水，颜色一缕缕散开。

branches.en: a scarf and gloves in the same deep shade
branches.cn: 同一种深色的围巾与手套

branches.en: walls that look black at night
branches.cn: 夜里几乎像黑色的墙面

branches.en: a robe that only one family could pay for
branches.cn: 只有一家人买得起的袍子

branches.en: a novel dressed up in decoration
branches.cn: 打扮得过分的小说

branches.en: a dye so costly that it named both a colour and a rank
branches.cn: 昂贵到同时命名了颜色与地位的染料

intro.en: A Greek noun for the shellfish and its dye holds the word together, and Latin, Old English and English endings carry it into colour, cloth and style.
intro.cn: 表示贝类及其染料的希腊语名词支撑着这个词，拉丁语、古英语与英语的词形再把它带到颜色、布匹与文风上。

latinIntro.en: Latin purpura, the dye and the cloth, and the verb purpurare, to dye purple, come from Greek porphyra and stand behind the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 purpura（染料与紫布）与动词 purpurare（染紫）来自希腊语 porphyra，是英语这个词的来源。

items.meaning: the colour, or of that colour

definition_zh: 目的；意图；用途；决心；意义；宗旨
definition_en: the reason for which something is done, made or exists
core_image: 木匠在工作台上把一块木板摆正，用粉线弹出一条笔直的线，才落下第一锯
scene: 开工之前，工头把图纸摊在木板上，用手指按住那条基准线，说明这块料为什么要留厚两毫米。The purpose of the extra thickness was to allow a second plane pass.
sceneCN: 这里 purpose 指「做某件事所依据的目的」（第 1 个义项：意图与目的）；句意为多留那两毫米是为了还能再刨一次。图中可辨识物件：摊开的图纸、按住基准线的手指、弹过粉线的木板、留下的余量；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 目的；意图；用途；决心；意义；宗旨
（较少用）打算；意图

derivatives.zh: 由名词加表示「充满」的形容词后缀构成，语义由「目的」转为「有明确目的的」
由名词加副词后缀构成，语义由「意图」转为「故意地」
加表示「缺少」的形容词后缀构成，语义由「目的」转为「没有目的的」
由名词与过去分词复合而成，语义由「用途」转为「专为某用途建造的」
加表示「多」的前缀构成，语义由「用途」转为「一物多用的」

senses.title: The reason for an act
senses.titleCN: 做一件事的理由与意图
senses.definition: the reason one has in mind for doing something or for making something
senses.definitionCN: 做某事或造某物时心里所抱的理由
senses.example: The purpose of the extra thickness was to allow a second plane pass.
senses.exampleCN: 多留那两毫米，是为了还能再刨一次。
senses.why: the word comes from putting something forward, so a purpose is the aim a person sets in front of the work before starting it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自「把某物摆到前面」，因此目的就是开工前把目标摆在工作前面的那件事。

senses.title: The function of a thing
senses.definition: the job that an object or a part is designed to perform
senses.definitionCN: 一件物件或部件被造出来所要承担的功能
senses.example: This room has outlived its original purpose as a laundry.
senses.exampleCN: 这间屋子原本用作洗衣房，如今那个用途早已过去了。
senses.why: the aim moves from the maker's head into the made thing, where it becomes a function.
senses.whyCN: 目标从造物者的脑子里移到被造之物里，在那里它就成了一种功能。

senses.title: Firmness of intention
senses.definition: resolute determination to carry out what one has decided
senses.definitionCN: 把已经决定的事做到底的那份坚决
senses.example: He spoke with purpose and nobody interrupted.
senses.exampleCN: 他说话带着决心，没人打断。
senses.why: a settled intention shows in the manner of speech, and the noun then names the firmness rather than the aim.
senses.whyCN: 已定的意图会显现在说话的方式上，此时名词指的是那份坚定，而不是目标。

senses.title: Relevance to the matter
senses.definition: the quality of bearing on the question at hand, as in remarks that are to the purpose
senses.definitionCN: 与眼前问题相干的品质，如「切题」的话
senses.example: Every question was to the purpose, and the meeting ended early.
senses.exampleCN: 每个问题都切中正题，会议提前结束。
senses.why: what is aimed at the matter in hand is relevant, so a fixed phrase marks this older, narrower sense.
senses.whyCN: 对准眼前事务的就是相关的，因此一个固定说法保存了这条更窄的旧义。

senses.title: Meaning in a life
senses.definition: the sense that one's existence or work has a point worth serving
senses.definitionCN: 觉得自己的存在或工作有一个值得效力的要点
senses.example: Teaching gave her a purpose she had not found in the laboratory.
senses.exampleCN: 教书给了她一种在实验室里没找到的意义。
senses.why: when the aim is large enough to organize a life, the word shifts from a task to a reason for living.
senses.whyCN: 当目标大到足以组织一生，这个词就从一项任务转为活着的理由。

senses.title: A stated aim of an institution
senses.definition: the declared aim that a body, a fund or a law is set up to serve
senses.definitionCN: 一个机构、基金或法律被设立时所声明的目标
senses.example: The fund's purpose is written on its first page.
senses.exampleCN: 这只基金的宗旨写在第一页上。
senses.why: organizations must put their aim forward in writing, which keeps the original image of placing something in front.
senses.whyCN: 机构必须把目标写在前面，这保留了「把某物摆到前面」的原初意象。

senses.title: Result actually achieved
senses.definition: the outcome that an action actually produces, as in efforts that came to good purpose
senses.definitionCN: 一个行动实际产生的效果，如「见了效」的努力
senses.example: All the digging came to good purpose when the well struck water.
senses.exampleCN: 井里出水时，所有挖掘都见了效。
senses.why: an aim that is realized becomes a result, and older English used the noun for that realized effect.
senses.whyCN: 实现的目标会变成结果，旧时英语就用这个名词指那种已实现的效用。

senses.title: A proposal or intent
senses.definition: a plan or proposal one puts forward, the sense closest to the French source
senses.definitionCN: 一个人摆出来的计划或提议，是最贴近法语来源的一层
senses.example: Their purpose was to rebuild the mill before winter.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的打算是在入冬前把磨坊重建起来。
senses.why: the French ancestor meant a proposal put forward, and this plain sense still surfaces in formal writing.
senses.whyCN: 法语祖词意为「摆出来的提议」，这一朴素义仍会在正式文字中浮现。

intro.en: Purpose comes through Old French porpos 'aim, intention' from porposer 'to put forth', a variant of proposer, which rests on Latin proponere 'to put forward', built on pro- 'forward' and ponere 'to place'. The deeper origin of ponere is not settled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 该词经古法语 porpos「目标、意图」来自 porposer「摆出、提出」，那是 proposer 的变体，其源头是拉丁 proponere「放到前面」，由 pro-「向前」与 ponere「放置」构成。ponere 的更深来源尚无定论，年代均为约数。

items.en: Ponere meant 'to put, place, set'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the proposal that links it to a root for 'to place' is circular and adds nothing, so the source is best left open.
items.cn: ponere 意为「放、置、摆」。其更深来源不确定；把它与另一个同样表示「放置」的词根相联系只是循环解释，并无增益，因此来源宜存疑。

items.en: Pro- 'forward' plus ponere gave proponere 'to put forward, set before one', used of plans, terms and proposals.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 ponere 构成 proponere「摆到前面、置于眼前」，用于计划、条款与提议。

items.en: Old French porposer 'to put forth, intend' produced the noun porpos, which named both the aim and the resolve behind it.
items.cn: 古法语 porposer「提出、打算」产生名词 porpos，兼指目标与背后的决心。

items.en: Middle English took purpose for an intention, and the phrase on purpose later fixed the sense of doing something deliberately.
items.cn: 中古英语用这个词表示意图，后来固定说法「故意地」把「有意为之」的意思定了下来。

items.en: Modern law and administration use the noun for the declared aim of a body, which is the oldest image of putting an aim in front of the work.
items.cn: 现代法律与行政用这个名词指机构声明的宗旨，这正是「把目标摆在工作前面」最古老的意象。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin of ponere and the exact date of the deliberateness phrase): no citation fixes the first use for an institution's aim, and any Indo-European form offered for ponere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（ponere 的更深来源与「故意」说法确切成形的年代）：机构宗旨义没有确切的最早书证；凡为 ponere 给出的印欧语形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one separates verbs and nouns built on the same placing root; group two separates words for an aim by how explicit it is.
note.cn: 第一组区分同出「放置」词根的动词与名词；第二组按明确程度区分表示「目标」的词。

entries.definition: The direct relative: to put a plan or an offer before others, from the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 最直接的同族词：把计划或提议摆到别人面前，同出那个拉丁动词。

entries.definition: From the same placing verb through French: to put something forward, hence to set a question or hold a position.
entries.definitionCN: 同出那个「放置」动词经法语而来：把某物摆出，因而指提出问题或摆出姿势。

entries.definition: In- 'upon' plus ponere: to place a burden on someone, which is the same root pressing downward.
entries.definitionCN: 由 in-「在上」加 ponere 构成：把负担压在别人身上，同一词根往下用力。

entries.definition: Com- 'together' plus ponere: to put parts together, hence to write or to calm oneself.
entries.definitionCN: 由 com-「共同」加 ponere 构成：把部件放到一起，因而指写作或使镇定。

entries.definition: From pro- plus portare 'to carry': to carry a meaning or a claim, with no placing involved and no shared root.
entries.definitionCN: 由 pro- 加 portare「搬运」构成：承载某种含义或声称，不含「放置」，也不同根。

entries.definition: The thing one intends to hit or reach; it is sharper and more specific than purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 打算击中或抵达的东西；比 purpose 更尖锐、更具体。

entries.definition: A defined end point one can mark and check; purpose is broader and can be a reason rather than a finish line.
entries.definitionCN: 一个可标示、可核对的明确终点；purpose 更宽，可以是理由而非终点线。

entries.definition: What a person means to do, often before acting; it is closer to the mental state than to the thing served.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人打算做什么，多在行动之前；更接近心理状态，而不是所服务的事。

entries.definition: The explanation of why something is as it is; it can look backward, while purpose looks forward.
entries.definitionCN: 解释某事为何如此的理由；可以向后看，而 purpose 向前看。

entries.definition: The work a thing performs; it is the mechanical face of purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 一件东西所执行的工作；是 purpose 在机械层面的面孔。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means to place, and the prefix means forward: a purpose is an aim placed in front of the work.
normal.cn: 词根意为「放置」，前缀意为「向前」：目的就是被摆在工作前面的那个目标。

normal.en: The family runs purpose, purposeful, purposely, purposeless, purpose-built, multipurpose.
normal.cn: 同族词覆盖名词、形容词、副词、否定式与两个复合词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: on purpose, serve a purpose, fit for purpose, a sense of purpose.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：故意地、起作用、适合用途、目标感。

normal.en: The siblings propose, pose, impose and compose all come from the same placing verb.
normal.cn: 同族的 propose、pose、impose 与 compose 都出自那个「放置」动词。

normal.en: The look-alike purport comes from a verb meaning to carry, so it means to claim rather than to intend.
normal.cn: 形近的 purport 出自一个意为「搬运」的动词，所以它的意思是「声称」而非「打算」。

abstract.en: Picture a chalk line snapped on a board before the first cut.
abstract.cn: 想象第一锯之前，木板上先弹出的一条粉线。

abstract.en: Picture a sign at the head of a path saying what the path is for.
abstract.cn: 想象一条小路的起点立着一块牌子，写着这条路是为什么修的。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp aimed at one desk rather than lighting the whole room.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯只照一张桌子，而不是照亮整间屋子。

examples.en: The purpose of the new rule is to slow the traffic at the gate.
examples.cn: 新规定的目的是让门口的车辆慢下来。

examples.en: He knocked the cup over on purpose and then apologized.
examples.cn: 他故意碰倒杯子，然后又道了歉。

examples.en: The building has served its purpose and will be pulled down.
examples.cn: 这座楼已经完成它的用途，将被拆除。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「purpose 破的」——先想清楚为什么做，才不容易把事情做破 → 目的

root: 古法语 porpos「目标、意图」← porposer「提出」← 拉丁 proponere「放到前面」= pro-（向前）+ ponere（放置）；ponere 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: an aim is placed in front of the work, and that placed aim then becomes a function, a firmness, a relevance, a reason for living, an institutional charter, a realized effect and finally a plain proposal.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：先把目标摆到工作前面，这个被摆出的目标随后变成一项功能、一份坚定、一种相关性、一个活着的理由、一纸机构宗旨、一个已实现的效果，最后成为一句朴素的提议。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a snapped chalk line laid on a board before the saw goes in.
core.cn: 核心意象：锯子落下之前，先在被板上弹出一条粉线。

branches.en: THE AIM PUT FORWARD: an intention in the mind and a proposal spoken aloud.
branches.cn: 摆出的目标：心里的意图与说出口的提议。

branches.en: THE AIM BUILT IN: one aim settles into a thing's function, another into a body's charter.
branches.cn: 被造进去的目标：一个目标落成物的功能，另一个落成机构的宗旨。

branches.en: THE AIM HELD TIGHT: resolve is the same aim felt as will.
branches.cn: 被握紧的目标：决心就是同一个目标在意志层面的感受。

branches.en: AIMED AND REALIZED: what bears on the matter, and what actually comes of it.
branches.cn: 对准与实现：切中事务的，以及确实做出来的效果。

branches.en: AIM LARGE ENOUGH FOR A LIFE: the aim becomes a reason to get up.
branches.cn: 大到足够撑起一生的目标：目标变成起床的理由。

intro.en: Purpose is a French-shaped noun whose Latin prefix and verb are still productive in English, so its parts can be read clearly.
intro.cn: 这个词是法语形态的名词，其拉丁前缀与动词在英语里仍有构成力，因此部件读得很清楚。

latinIntro.en: Latin ponere 'to place' gives propose, impose, compose, position and deposit; pro- 'forward' appears in proceed, promote and protect.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ponere「放置」衍生出 propose、impose、compose、position 与 deposit；pro-「向前」见于 proceed、promote 与 protect。

items.example: The prefix puts the aim ahead of the act.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把目标放在行动之前。
这个词根提供「放置」的动作。

items.example: The plan was put forward at the meeting.
items.exampleCN: 计划在会上被提了出来。

items.example: The purpose was written on the first page.
A purposeful walk covered the ridge by noon.
items.exampleCN: 一次有目的的行走在正午前走完了山脊。

items.example: She purposely left the door open.

items.exampleCN: 没有目的的挖掘毁了草坪。

items.example: A purpose-built studio replaced the shed.
items.exampleCN: 一间专用工作室取代了棚屋。

items.example: A multipurpose hall serves the whole village.
items.exampleCN: 一座多用途大厅供全村使用。
他们提出了一条更短的路线。

definition_zh: 钱包；女式手袋；财力；资金；奖金
definition_en: a small bag used for carrying money, especially a woman's handbag; also the money a person or group has available, or the prize money offered in a competition
core_image: 围裙内袋里一只磨旧的皮钱袋，装着一整天的收入
scene: 早市快收摊时，卖菜的女人把零钱一张张理平，塞进围裙内侧的布袋。She kept the day's takings in a worn leather purse.
sceneCN: 这里 purse 是「钱包、随身钱袋」（第 1 个义项：装钱的小包）；句意为她把一天的收入放进一只磨旧的皮钱包里。画面里可留意：围裙、理平的零钱、旧皮袋。

pos.zh: 钱包；女式手袋；财力；资金；奖金

derivatives.zh: purse 加表人后缀 -er，原指管钱袋的人，现指船上掌管账目与薪水的职务
cut 与 purse 复合，字面是「割钱袋的人」，指旧时的扒手
purse 与 proud 复合，指因富有而傲慢的

senses.title: A small bag for carrying money
senses.definition: a small bag, often with a clasp, used especially by women for carrying money and a few personal items
senses.definitionCN: 尤指女性使用、常带扣合的小包，用来装钱和少量随身物品
senses.example: She took a coin from her purse and paid the driver.
senses.exampleCN: 她从钱包里取出一枚硬币付给司机。
senses.why: The Latin word behind it named a leather bag, and the first English purses were soft pouches pulled shut with strings, long before notes and cards existed.
senses.whyCN: 它背后的拉丁词本指皮袋，英语最早的 purse 就是用细绳收口的小软袋，那时还没有纸币和银行卡。

senses.title: The money a person or group can spend
senses.definition: the amount of money that a person, family or organization has available to spend
senses.definitionCN: 个人、家庭或机构手头可供支配的钱
senses.example: The repair cost more than the family purse could bear.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔修缮费超出了这个家庭的财力。
senses.why: Once a container holds money, the container can stand for the contents, and then for the spending power those contents give.
senses.whyCN: 容器一旦装着钱，就能代指里面的钱，再进一步指这些钱带来的购买力。

senses.title: Prize money in a competition
senses.definition: the sum of money offered as a prize in a race, a fight or another contest
senses.definitionCN: 赛跑、拳赛或其他比赛中作为奖品的钱
senses.example: The boxer gave his purse to the village school.
senses.exampleCN: 这名拳手把奖金捐给了村里的学校。
senses.why: Prize money was once handed over in an actual bag at the end of a contest, so the name of the container stayed on the prize after payments moved to cheques.
senses.whyCN: 比赛结束时奖金真的装在一只袋子里当场交付，所以即使后来改用支票，容器之名仍留在奖金上。

intro.en: Purse travels back through Old French and medieval Latin to Latin bursa, a leather bag; the Greek word behind bursa is generally thought to be a borrowing, so anything deeper is uncertain.
intro.cn: purse 经古法语与中世纪拉丁语上溯到拉丁语 bursa（皮袋）；bursa 背后的希腊词一般认为也是借词，再往前的来源并不确定。

items.en: Greek byrsa meant a hide or a leather bag, and it is generally considered a loanword into Greek rather than an inherited item.
items.cn: 希腊语 byrsa 指兽皮或皮袋，一般认为它是借入希腊语的词，而非本土传承。

items.en: Latin bursa named a leather pouch and later a treasury or money chest, which is why the family also touches public money.
items.cn: 拉丁语 bursa 指皮制小袋，后来也指金库、钱柜，所以这个词族也涉及公共资金。

items.en: Medieval Latin kept bursa for a bag and a treasury, while Old French developed borse, the form that carried the word towards England.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语保留 bursa 指袋子和金库，古法语则发展出 borse，正是把这个词带向英格兰的形式。

items.en: Middle English purs named a small drawstring pouch worn at the belt, carried by men as well as women.
items.cn: 中古英语 purs 指系在腰带上、用细绳收口的小袋，男女都常佩带。

items.en: Everyday modern English narrows the object to a woman's handbag, while the older sense of available money survives in public purse and purse strings.
items.cn: 现代英语日常用法把这个物件收窄为女式手袋，而「可用之钱」的旧义仍活在 public purse 与 purse strings 里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects spellings and relatives built on the same bag word; the near-meaning group collects other words for what holds money or for money itself.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「袋」词上的拼写与同族词；近义组收其他表示装钱的物件或钱本身的词。

entries.definition: To follow someone in order to catch them; only the opening letters are similar.
entries.definitionCN: 追赶、追求；只是开头几个字母相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The officer on a ship who keeps the accounts and pays the crew.
entries.definitionCN: 船上负责账目与发放薪水的职务。

entries.definition: An official who manages money in a college or school.
entries.definitionCN: 在大学或学校里管理钱财的职务。

entries.definition: To pay money back to someone who has spent it on your behalf.
entries.definitionCN: 把别人替你垫付的钱还给他。

entries.definition: A small flat case for notes and cards, usually carried in a pocket.
entries.definitionCN: 装纸币与卡片的小扁夹，通常放在口袋里。

entries.definition: A bag for personal items, carried especially by women.
entries.definitionCN: 装随身物品的包，尤指女性提包。

entries.definition: Money set aside for a particular purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 为某个用途准备的钱。

entries.definition: A shared sum of money collected from a group.
entries.definitionCN: 一群人凑起来共用的一笔钱。

normalIntro.en: The word goes back to a leather bag, and every later sense still keeps something of that one small container.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词源自一只皮袋，后来每个义项都还留着那只小容器的影子。

normal.en: Bursa in Latin is a leather pouch, and the earliest English purses were exactly that: soft bags closed with string.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 bursa 是皮制小袋，英语最早的 purse 正是这种用细绳收口的软袋。

normal.en: Purser keeps the money-handling side of the family: the person on a ship who looks after accounts and pay.
normal.cn: purser 保留了词族中「管钱」的一面：船上负责账目与薪水的人。

normal.en: Reimburse puts re- (back) with a stem from bursa, so the word pictures money going back into the bag it came from.
normal.cn: reimburse 把表示「回」的 re- 与 bursa 的词干结合，画面就是钱回到原来的袋子里。

normal.en: Purse strings were once literal cords; holding them now means controlling the money itself.
normal.cn: purse strings 从前是实实在在的绳子，如今握住它就等于掌控钱财。

normal.en: The public purse treats a whole country's funds as one bag that officials must open with care.
normal.cn: public purse 把一个国家的资金看成一只袋子，官员打开它时必须谨慎。

abstract.en: A purse fits in one hand, yet it can stand for everything a household is able to choose.
abstract.cn: 钱袋一只手就握得住，却可以代表一个家庭所能做的一切选择。

abstract.en: One word names the bag, the money and the prize, because each is something handed from one person to another.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指袋子、又指钱和奖金，因为这三样都是从一个人手里交到另一个人手里。

abstract.en: A purse is often closed not by its clasp but by the fear behind it.
abstract.cn: 钱袋往往是靠背后的顾虑合上的，而不是靠那道扣子。

examples.en: She paid the fare from a small purse she kept in her coat.
examples.cn: 她用外套里一只小钱包付了车费。

examples.en: The tour was cancelled because the club's purse was empty.
examples.cn: 巡演取消了，因为俱乐部的资金已经见底。

examples.en: The winner took home a purse of fifty thousand dollars.
examples.cn: 冠军拿走了五万美元奖金。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「珀斯」——去澳大利亚的珀斯旅行，得先备好钱包，记住 purse 是钱包、财力。

root: 拉丁语 bursa（皮袋、钱袋）经中世纪拉丁语与古法语进入中古英语作 purs；同族词多与袋、钱、偿付有关，如 purser、reimburse。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a bag that holds money; the senses divide into the bag itself, the money inside it, and the prize once handed over in such a bag.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是装钱的袋子；义项由此分为袋子本身、袋里的钱，以及从前装在这种袋子里交付的奖金。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a worn leather pouch tucked inside an apron, holding a whole day's earnings.
core.cn: 核心意象：围裙内侧一只磨旧的皮袋，装着一整天的收入。

branches.en: a drawstring pouch on a market stall
branches.cn: 集市摊前一只收口的钱袋

branches.en: a bag whose weight equals a family's choices
branches.cn: 一只袋子的分量等于一个家庭的选择

branches.en: a council counting what it can afford
branches.cn: 市政会算着手里的钱够做什么

branches.en: a prize handed over in a leather bag
branches.cn: 装在皮袋里当场交付的奖金

branches.en: money that is both kept and awarded
branches.cn: 既被存着又被颁出去的同一笔钱

intro.en: The word is held together by a Greek bag word, its Latin descendant, the English noun, and the suffixes that build a person and a paying-back verb.
intro.cn: 这个词由希腊语的「袋」、它的拉丁后裔、英语名词，以及构成「人」与「偿付」的后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。
